articles.title: Sara Duterte, husband's 'unexplained wealth' could reach P1.5B --witness
articles.summary: The unexplained wealth of Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio, could reach P1.5 billion at the maximum and P817 million at the minimum, lawyer and certified public accountant…

blocks.text: Published October 12, 2026 6:52pm

The unexplained wealth of Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio, could reach P1.5 billion at the maximum and P817 million at the minimum, lawyer and certified public accountant Alex Cabrera said Monday.

The prosecution’s witness made the testimony during Day 38 of the impeachment trial of the Vice President, assuring that his team did not make any double recording or double entry in its forensic investigation of the Vice President and her husband’s bank records, bank transactions, income tax returns, financial statements and other corporate records.

“I did not include confidential funds, which is P475 million. Our discrepancy with AMLC, if we are not going to be conservative, would be P100 million. For GenCorp. [undeclared sales], if we use 45%, that would be P250 million. So P350 million plus P475 million is P700 million,” Cabrera said when asked by Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero what his estimates would be, ceiling-wise, rather than the conservative estimate which is just at P817 million in total.
Asked what would be the ceiling amount, Cabrera said, “P1.5 billion.”
Asked by Escudero whether the amount will go down if the couple accounts for tax dues, Cabrera answered in the affirmative.
“If there are payables, we will deduct that from that (P1.5 billion) amount,” Cabrera said.
Cabrera also assured that his findings of P817 unexplained wealth from 2022 to 2025 are conservative or bare minimum, and that there are no double entries.

“These are all official documents. We meticulously reviewed them. Four eyes, six-yes review, and we used software technology in comparing records. We made sure that a remittance is not for two accounts. We made sure of that,” he said.
“In case of doubt or making an error, we don’t include it. Because if we have double entries, our estimate would exceed,” he added. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Balkan temperatures swing as heavy rain heads for Greece
articles.summary: Clear skies bring warm days and cold nights to Montenegro, while a low-pressure system moves towards Aegean Sea
articles.byline: Ed Walton and James Parrish for MetDesk

blocks.text: Temperatures fluctuated dramatically in the Balkans last week, with unusually large differences between daytime highs and overnight lows – known as the diurnal range.

An area of high pressure over the region brought prolonged sunshine during the day, while clear skies at night allowed temperatures to drop rapidly as heat escaped into the atmosphere without cloud cover to slow the cooling.

In Kosanica, Montenegro, the average maximum temperature in October is 15C (59F), while the average minimum is 4C. However, on 4 and 5 October the difference between daytime highs and overnight lows reached 30C, more than double the October average.

Elsewhere in Europe, high pressure will build across the north and west over the coming week, pushing an area of low pressure southwards towards the Mediterranean. The low-pressure system will deepen as it crosses the Adriatic and Ionian seas before moving eastwards into the Aegean Sea by the middle of the week.

Spells of heavy rain and strong winds are expected to sweep across Greece as a result. Forecast models suggest widespread rainfall of 50-150mm, with the highest totals expected around the island of Skiathos.

Towards the end of the week, the system will continue eastwards, bringing showers to parts of Crete, which was hit by severe flooding a week earlier. Those storms swept some cars and trees into the sea.

blocks.caption: People cross a bridge over a swollen river as Hurricane Simon approaches Mexico’s Pacific coast in Costalegre, Jalisco state. Photograph: Daniel Becerril/Reuters

blocks.text: Meanwhile, Hurricane Simon, a category 4 storm, is moving close to Mexico’s Pacific coast, near the state of Jalisco. It is the latest of 21 named storms in the Pacific this season, 11 of which have reached hurricane strength.

At the time of writing, Simon has a central pressure of 933mb and maximum sustained winds of nearly 150mph (241km/h). However, the hurricane is expected to weaken rapidly if its core moves onshore, cutting it off from the warm ocean waters that fuel it.

articles.title: Germany's Wadephul calls new EU sanctions 'unprecedented' blow to Russia
articles.summary: The European Union has approved its largest-ever sanctions package against Moscow, targeting more than 1,000 entities tied to the military-industrial complex.

image.caption: Businesses and individuals tied to missile production were named in this group of sanctions in particularImage: Alexei Konovalov/ZUMA/IMAGO

blocks.text: German foreign Minister Johann Wadephul described a new raft of punitive measures against Russia as an "unprecedented sanction blow" to President Vladimir Putin's war in Ukraine.

"We are making it harder for Putin to continue his war of aggression in violation of international law, and his cynical attempt to wear down Ukraine's civilian population through murderous bombing campaigns," Wadephul said on Monday as EU foreign ministers met in Luxembourg to finalize the sanctions package.
Who do the sanctions target?
It targets some 1,600 individuals and businesses related to Russia's war effort, and another 77 people and groups related to what the EU sees as illegal elections in occupied Ukrainian terrorities.

EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said in a post on X that this was "the single largest expansion of our sanctions list since Russia started its war...More than half are connected to the production chain for ballistic missiles."
"We are making it significantly harder, slower and more expensive for Russia to produce the weapons it uses to kill Ukrainians," she added.
Although he could not attend the Luxembourg meeting due to a party conference in Berlin, Wadephul said: "The message is clear: Russia cannot and will not win this war."
However, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk appeared to imply that sanctions need to go even further as the conflict was set to enter its fifth bitter winter.

"This is the moment when the entire West...should show Russia and Putin that it is ready to pursue a policy of containing Russia by even more decisive means," he told the Warsaw Security Forum, referring to EU sanctions. "That is why I will go to Brussels to persuade all our European partners to seriously consider increasing sanctions against Russia.
What is the latest development in the war?
Russian forces have repeatedly stepped up attacks on Ukraine's critical energy infrastructure every autumn since its invasion, hoping to cripple heating and other necessary utilitiesahead of winter.

US President Donald Trump declared that there was an "energy ceasefire" in place between Russia and Ukraine over the weekend. However, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he had no idea what Trump was referring to and that Russia had continued to target energy facilities unabated.

articles.title: Zelenskyy vows to retaliate if Russian strikes on Ukraine’s power grid continue
articles.summary: Ukrainian president says at Warsaw summit Trump’s ‘energy ceasefire’ post, as Kyiv struck by Russian drones, ‘surprised’ him
articles.byline: Andrew Roth in Kyiv, Jennifer Rankin in Brussels and Luke Harding

blocks.text: Volodymyr Zelenskyy has vowed to respond to Russia’s continuing attacks on the Ukrainian power grid as European leaders rally around Kyiv amid a feud with Donald Trump over Ukraine’s strikes on oil refineries.

Speaking to a gathering of European security officials in Warsaw on Monday, the Ukrainian president said Ukraine would retaliate if strikes on its power grid continued: “If Russia does not agree to an energy ceasefire this winter, we will respond.”

On Sunday Trump announced an “energy ceasefire” between Kyiv and Moscow that Zelenskyy said neither side had agreed to. On Monday, Zelenskyy said he was “surprised” by the post, which went online while Kyiv was being attacked by Russian Shahed drones.

blocks.caption: Attendees at a Warsaw security summit on Monday watch Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s address on a large screen. Photograph: Attila Husejnow/AP

blocks.text: Russia then launched a “targeted attack” on a Kharkiv power station just hours later, as much of Kyiv was plunged into darkness. “It’s clear that Putin does not read Truth Social,” Zelenskyy quipped.

Ukraine wants to negotiate an energy ceasefire that would take the pressure off its electricity grid before the winter. Russia has so far been unwilling to halt its attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure.
European leaders have voiced support for Kyiv in the feud, saying Russia was responsible for the continuing strikes on energy infrastructure in both countries.

“We welcome the energy ceasefire when it holds,” the EU foreign policy chief, Kaja Kallas, said at a meeting of European foreign ministers on Monday. “We haven’t yet seen that also Russia will stick to it.”

Ministers from the Baltic states criticised a US decision to lift sanctions on imports of Russian diesel, which had been blocked as part of punishment for Putin launching the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

“This deal doesn’t help, neither the crisis of the oil products, nor the unity within the transatlantic community when it concerns Russia,” said Lithuania’s foreign minister, Keʂtutis Budrys. “And it is not the European way. Our way is to increase pressure because we already see how it works.”

Russia has increased its attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure, using jet-powered drones and ballistic missiles ahead of the cold winter months, leading to blackouts and water shortages far earlier in the season than has been usual during the war.
Trump’s proposal was for both sides to halt strikes on oil refineries but Kallas said that deal favoured Russia, which has far more refineries.
Trump has blamed the high price of diesel on Ukraine’s attacks, rather than the global shock to energy markets from the war in Iran and the subsequent closure of the strait of Hormuz.

The fast-moving row between Washington and Kyiv began on Friday when Trump announced he was lifting sanctions on Russian diesel exports. He said the move would reduce global and domestic fuel prices before next month’s US midterm elections.

A furious Zelenskyy called the decision “weak” and said it would generate “billions” in extra revenue for Putin, enabling him to wage war “even more intensely”. An equally irate Trump said Zelenskyy should “damn well stop” hitting Russian refineries. Ukraine needed a “new leader”, he said on Saturday.

Responding to Trump, Zelenskyy said it was up to Ukrainians to choose “one or another leader”. He told ABC News he was willing to accept Trump’s demands and to organise elections, but only if Putin agreed to a “total” 60-day ceasefire.

articles.title: PDEA: 2 Filipinos under investigation over PH-bound shabu seized in Laos
articles.summary: The Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA) on Monday confirmed that two Filipinos are being linked to the alleged attempt to smuggle 521 kilograms of suspected methamphetamine hydrochloride, or…

blocks.text: Published October 12, 2026 6:30pm

The Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA) on Monday confirmed that two Filipinos are being linked to the alleged attempt to smuggle 521 kilograms of suspected methamphetamine hydrochloride, or shabu, from Laos to the Philippines via a private jet.
At a press conference, PDEA Director General Isagani Nerez said alias “Fahad” was arrested at an airport in Laos in connection with the alleged smuggling of drugs.

“Si Fahad, confirmed na Pilipino siya. Yung residence niya ngayon is in Marawi. Meron na tayong listahan kung saan pa yung mga ibang place of residence niya. 'Yan na ngayon ang focus ng ating investigation dahil siya nakapulong ngayon doon,” Nerez said.

(We have confirmed that he is a Filipino. His current residence is in Marawi. We also have a list of his other places of residence, which is the focus of our investigation, as he is currently detained there.)
“But the challenge is we have to establish yung link, sino mga kakuntsaba niya sa Pilipinas (who are his accomplices in the Philippines),” he added.
Meanwhile, alias “Boyet” allegedly arranged the private jet to transport drugs from Laos to the Philippines.
“We have evidence that si Boyet is taga-dito sa Luzon at si Fahad may address sa Luzon parehas po. So that makes sense. It will establish yung link nila na magkakilala,” Nerez said.
(We have evidence that Boyet is from Luzon and that Fahad also has an address in Luzon. This makes sense, as it could establish a link between the two and show that they know each other.)
“Alam namin he's affiliated doon sa drug group na sinusundan namin. Dahil kaibigan niya yung nag-charter ng eroplano na yung tao na ’yan si Boyet ay nasa listahan ng PDEA,” he added.
(We know he is affiliated with the drug group we are monitoring because he is friends with the person who chartered the aircraft. Boyet is also on the PDEA’s watchlist.)
Boyet was reportedly flown to Hong Kong, according to Nerez.
The PDEA official said authorities have information about Fahad’s accomplices in the Philippines but did not go into the details since it is under investigation.
Once authorities establish their identities, Nerez said the next step would be to build cases against them.
He added that Philippine authorities are also seeking more information from their counterparts in Laos about the smuggled drugs.

Initial information showed that the Learjet flew from Malaysia to Laos to pick up 23 pieces of luggage containing illegal drugs, but authorities discovered the drugs after the pilot refused to load them.
Nerez said Fahad could face penalties, including the death penalty, if proven to be involved in drug smuggling. –NB, GMA News

articles.title: FACT CHECK: Quote card of Escudero, Luistro on impeachment trial witnesses is fake
articles.summary: There are no credible news reports or videos from the impeachment trial showing that they explicitly made the remarks shown in the false post

blocks.text: Claim: A quote card features impeachment trial presiding officer Senator Francis “Chiz” Escudero telling the House lead prosecutor, Batangas 2nd District Representative Gerville Luistro, that they cannot halt the impeachment proceedings against Vice President Sara Duterte after initiating them. In response, Luistro said the prosecution no longer had any witnesses to present.

Why we fact-checked this: One Facebook reel bearing the claim has already received 860,000 views, 15,800 reactions, 1,400 shares, and 1,200 comments as of writing. While the reel was posted on September 15, it continues to gain traction with a new comment posted on October 10.

The post features photos of Escudero and Luistro and quotes attributed to the two. It cites Escudero — falsely identified in the post as Supreme Court Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo — supposedly saying, “Atty. Luistro hindi pwede itigil ang trial na inumpisahan nyo.”
(Atty. Luistro, you cannot stop the trial you initiated.)
Luistro’s alleged response was, “Wala na kasi kami maipresentang witness.”
(We no longer have any witnesses to present.)

Most of the comments believed that the statements were from a real discussion during Duterte’s impeachment trial. One commenter wrote, “Wala pa nga silang napatunayan ni isa, puro gawa gawa lang wala naman napatunayan.”
(They haven’t proven a single thing. It’s all just made-up, nothing has actually been proven).

The facts: Escudero and Luistro did not make the statements shown in the quote card. There are no credible news reports or videos from the impeachment trial showing that they explicitly made the remarks shown in the false post.

The closest similar statement was the remark Escudero jokingly made last July: “Hindi tayo matitigil dito, Gerville, sinasabi ko sa’yo (We won’t be able to finish this session, Gerville, I’m telling you),” when Luistro made a follow-up manifestation during the impeachment trial. Escudero then allowed Luistro to state her manifestation.

Meanwhile, Luistro did not make the remark about the prosecution “running out” of witnesses. The Batangas lawmaker, however, earlier made statements about “having no other choice” when presenting hostile witnesses for the trial.

In a DZMM Teleradyo interview on September 21 on the presentation of Davao City Mayor Sebastian Duterte as witness, Luistro said, “In instances na nakikita niyo na ang pinepresent ng prosecution is hostile, it only means, wala na kaming choice. This is the only option left kaya napilitan na kaming ipresenta kahit hostile witness siya.”

(In instances where we see that the witness being presented by the prosecution is hostile, it simply means we have no other choice. This is the only remaining option, so we were compelled to present them, even though they are a hostile witness.)
Impeachment trial witnesses: The House lead prosecutor has earlier said that they will no longer present several witnesses due to various reasons.

In July, the prosecution dropped six witnesses on Article 4 of the impeachment case against Duterte to avoid redundancy as they deemed the testimony of National Bureau of Investigation Director Melvin Matibag already sufficient to prove the allegations.
Zuleika Lopez, Duterte’s chief of staff, as well as House security officer Belinda Bello, were also withdrawn as witnesses.
Former senator Antonio Trillanes IV, a Duterte critic, also requested to be removed from the list of witnesses so that the prosecution would be “relieved from the pressure it is going through.”

On October 9, the House prosecution panel said its final witness in Duterte’s impeachment trial was financial forensic analyst Alexander Cabrera, who told the impeachment court that the Vice President has P817 million in undeclared wealth. (LIVE UPDATES: Impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte)

Angelee Kaye Abelinde is a student journalist based in Naga City, and an alumna of Rappler’s Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship 2024.

articles.title: Saudi minister vows 'serious response' to Houthi attacks on airports
articles.summary: It comes after the armed group hit Riyadh's international airport and another facility, killing 13 people, in a significant escalation.

blocks.text: Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the government from Sanaa. The conflict escalated in 2015, after the Saudi-led coalition intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule.

A four-year-old informal ceasefire began to unravel in July, when the Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.

The Houthis said they were retaliating for what they say is a Saudi blockade of ports and airports in their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport that they blamed on the kingdom. The Yemeni government claimed it was behind that strike, saying it was trying to prevent an unauthorised Iranian plane from landing.

Last month, the Houthis launched a surprise offensive along Yemen's south-western Red Sea coast and ousted pro-government forces from areas overlooking the Bab al-Mandab Strait, at the southern end of the Red Sea.
They said they posed no threat to international shipping passing through the waterway but that they would continue to target vessels from Saudi Arabia.

However, the seizure of the strait contributed to a surge in global oil prices because Saudi Arabia had been relying on the Red Sea for oil exports after the US and Israel's war with Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz in the Gulf.
Last week, the Yemeni government announced the start of a new offensive aimed at retaking all territory held by the Houthis.
Pro-government forces said they were quickly able to retake areas around Bab al-Mandab with the help of intense Saudi air strikes, but the Houthis denied losing any territory.

articles.title: NBI probes 121 Duterte properties over alleged SALN discrepancies
articles.summary: The National Bureau of Investigation is probing 121 properties linked to Vice President Sara Duterte and her brother, Rep. Paolo Duterte, over discrepancies in their Statements of Assets, Liabilities…

blocks.text: October 12, 2026 | 6:26pm
National Bureau of Investigation Director Melvin Matibag speaks during a press briefing with reporters on Oct. 12, 2026.
The STAR / Mark Villeza

MANILA, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) is probing 121 properties linked to Vice President Sara Duterte and her brother, Rep. Paolo Duterte, over discrepancies in their Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALNs).

NBI Director Melvin Matibag said on Monday, October 12, that the probe stemmed from an affidavit by dismissed police officer Rudolfo Gracioso Jr., who claimed to have delivered suitcases of cash to the vice president.
Of the 121 properties linked to the Duterte family, 24 were declared in Sara Duterte’s SALN, Matibag said.
Alleged land banking
According to Matibag, citing Gracioso’s affidavit, several properties were declared as low-value agricultural land, but physical verification revealed high-end developments.

“Sagutin natin sa tao na bakit nag-declare tayo sa ating SALN na agricultural property, agricultural land property, may nakatayo pa lang mansion,” Matibag said in a press conference, referring to the Dutertes.
(Let us answer to the public why we declared in our SALN that it was an agricultural land property when a mansion is actually standing on it.)
“So, ito malinaw na 'yung pag hindi pag-de-declare pa lang ng tama sa SALN, meron na tayo dapat panagutan dito,” he added.
(So, this makes it clear that failing to declare correctly in the SALN alone is already grounds for accountability.)
Matibag cited a property in Barangay Catigan that was declared in the SALN with a value of only P890,000.

However, the NBI chief claimed that independent assessments and physical inspections by licensed property appraisers revealed that the actual value of the property, which features a mansion, swimming pools and a helipad, ranges from P14 million to P61 million.
The bureau also mentioned several properties in Samal and Davao.

Matibag said the bureau was drawing parallels with a previously established pattern in which large deliveries of money were allegedly used to acquire resorts, hotels, luxury villages and other real properties, as mentioned in Gracioso’s affidavit.
He added that all the initial reports obtained would be forwarded to the Office of the Ombudsman and the Department of Justice.
In response to the NBI's findings, Duterte said that every allegation against her was anchored on her announcement of her intention to run for president in the 2028 elections.
"Alam niyo napansin ko lang ha, lahat nalang ng illegal ay pinahid nila sa akin," Duterte said.
(You know, I've just noticed that they blame every single illegal thing on me.)

articles.title: Americans Hall and Woodford win Nobel economics prize for work on stabilization
articles.summary: The two developed new macroeconomic models that improved our ability to implement effective stabilization policy, enabling well-timed fiscal and monetary policy measures that can reduce the intensity…

blocks.text: LAUREATES. Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford are announced as the laureates of the 2026 Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel at the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences in Stockholm, Sweden, on October 12, 2026.
TT News Agency/Anders Wiklund via Reuters

The two developed new macroeconomic models that improved our ability to implement effective stabilization policy, enabling well-timed fiscal and monetary policy measures that can reduce the intensity of damaging swings in the economy

STOCKHOLM, Sweden – US academics Robert Hall and Michael Woodford won the 2026 Nobel economics prize “for microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilization,” the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences said on Monday, October 12.

The prestigious award, formally known as the Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel, is the final prize to be given out this year and is worth 12 million Swedish crowns ($1.2 million).

The two laureates developed new macroeconomic models that improved our ability to implement effective stabilization policy, enabling well-timed fiscal and monetary policy measures that can reduce the intensity of damaging swings in the economy.

“The laureates’ work has provided us with a stable theoretical foundation for the models that are now used by central banks and governments around the world,” John Hassler, Chair of the Committee for the Prize in Economic Sciences, said in a statement.
“With them, we are better equipped to deal with shocks in the economy, such as energy crises or sudden changes in how much households consume.”

The economics prize, first awarded in 1969, is not one of the original five awards created in the 1895 will of industrialist and dynamite inventor Alfred Nobel, but was established by Sweden’s central bank.

The majority of previous laureates have been from the United States. Only three women have ever won, most recently Claudia Goldin in 2023 for work on how gender has affected pay and employment over time in the United States.

Analysis by the Institute for Scientific Information, part of Clarivate, had picked researchers working on monetary policy, the economics of information technology and evolutionary economic theory as possible recipients.
Last year’s winners, Joel Mokyr, Philippe Aghion and Peter Howitt, won for work on “creative destruction” and how new technology and production methods can boost growth and living standards.
The Nobel prizes for medicine, physics, chemistry, literature and peace were announced last week. – Rappler.com

The change signals a softer stance by the Trump administration on international AI safety efforts, giving US developers greater latitude to cooperate with Britain as policymakers grapple with how to oversee AI

WASHINGTON, USA – American AI developers can give the British government early access to AI models for safety testing without running afoul of US President Donald Trump’s administration, the Telegraph newspaper said on Sunday, October 11.

The Trump administration has reversed a decision that requested developers such as OpenAI and Anthropic not to share new AI models with Britain’s AI Security Institute before release, the newspaper said.

The change signals a softer stance by the Trump administration on international AI safety efforts, giving US developers greater latitude to cooperate with Britain as policymakers grapple with how to oversee the increasingly powerful technology.
Spokespersons for Trump, OpenAI and Anthropic did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Reuters.
Britain’s AI Security Institute, set up after the world’s first AI safety summit in 2023, tests the most advanced AI models to evaluate their capabilities and the risk of misuse.
Trump has repeatedly dismissed calls for binding safety requirements on AI developers, a position that appears to be shifting.
His newly launched AI task force said on Friday developers must report security incidents with their AI models. – Rappler.com

articles.title: EU deal with China limits imports of hybrid electric vehicles
articles.summary: Brussels uses WTO rules to quickly impose 350,000 vehicle-a-year quota, which will halve Chinese market share to 3%

blocks.text: The EU is to limit the number of hybrid electrical vehicles imported from China to 350,000 cars a year, the European Commission has confirmed.
Imports have been soaring in the last two years with about 800,000 battery and plug-in hybrids likely to be sold this year.
The EU expects that the quota, which will come into force in December, will halve China’s market share which now stands at 6% in a landmark four-year agreement made in Beijing last week.

The annual limit on imports of hybrids will be taken under the World Trade Organization safeguard measures, which mean it can be implemented swiftly without the type of investigations needed in anti-dumping measures.
Any cars imported above the quota level will not be subject to tariffs, but will remain blocked in customs at docks in Europe.

Chinese vehicles or assembled within the EU, such as those made in Hungary or, in future, Spain, will not be subjected to the quota, officials have confirmed but EU companies making cars in China will be subjected to the quota.
As part of the deal, China has also agreed to drop some tariffs on auto parts and cut duties by half on footwear, olive oil and ice-cream from the EU.
Officials stressed that the quota is fully supported by China with further dialogue on cars and other imports including chemicals, renewable energy and furniture continuing.
“We will continue the dialogue on some products … this is by no means the end of the story,” said an official.
Last month the EU called for feedback on a new rule which could oblige companies to diversify their supply chains while theMade in Europe legislation would do the same in public procurement.

On Thursday EU leaders will discuss a French-German proposal for a “kill switch” or new instrument which would allow Brussels to block access to the single market for certain goods in the event of any harmful event, such as a ban on rare earths crucial for the tech and automotive industries.
after newsletter promotion
The deal on hybrid EVs comes amid mounting concern over the £1bn (€1.18bn) a day trade deficit the EU is now running with China.
Up until recently the EU’s strategy at tackling what they say is an “unsustainable” trade imbalance is to seek to increase imports to China.

Sources said there has been “a paradigm shift” with concerns of deindustrialisation and job losses in the industrial heartlands forcing a renewed focus on curbing imports rather than increasing exports.
“We are closely surveilling, our imports. We know what’s coming in. We know where there’s a surge, and we know what hits the hardest in terms of our deindustrialization,” said an official.

articles.title: Mans Carpio’s food firm shows money laundering symptoms — analyst
articles.summary: A food company linked to Vice President Sara Duterte’s husband, Manases “Mans” Carpio, showed symptoms of money laundering, forensic financial analyst Atty. Alexander Cabrera said…

blocks.text: October 12, 2026 | 6:08pm

MANILA, Philippines — A food company linked to Vice President Sara Duterte’s husband, Manases “Mans” Carpio, showed symptoms of money laundering, forensic financial analyst Atty. Alexander Cabrera said on Monday, October 12, citing large amounts of money flowing in and out of its accounts within a day or two.

Cale 88 Foods Corp., a supposed banana chip exporter, received P319.33 million in remittances from mainland China and Hong Kong, according to financial records presented during the Senate impeachment trial’s proceedings on Article II, which covers allegations of unexplained wealth against Vice President Sara Duterte.

The Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) confirmed the remittances before the Senate impeachment court on October 5, based on covered and suspicious transaction reports submitted by banks and financial institutions.

The money went into Cale 88’s corporate accounts, not directly into the personal accounts of Duterte or her husband, according to the AMLC records. Carpio reportedly held a 47.5% stake in the company from 2021 to 2024, according to its general information sheet.
Cabrera described Cale 88’s financial transactions as a “revolving door,” saying the money did not appear to add value to its business.

“That is a symptom of money laundering. Again, this is not in my report, and I am not saying that money laundering is taking place here. I am only saying that it is a symptom,” Cabrera said after Senator-judge Risa Hontiveros interjected during the hearing.
“When money enters the company and leaves on the same day or the following day, it means it has not added any value to the company,” he added.
Cabrera made the remarks after Senator-judge Raffy Tulfo asked him to explain his findings on Cale 88’s financial statements.

The company had no payables or receivables despite being a manufacturer or exporter of manufactured goods. It also had no inventory of raw materials or work in process, while continuing to incur losses regardless of the amount of money passing through its accounts, Cabrera said.
“What we see at Cale 88 is not tinikling; I would call it a revolving door. Money comes in and goes out. Large amounts of money flow in and out,” he said.

Cabrera said the transactions could indicate that Cale 88 was being used as a pass-through for funds under the pretense of business activity. He clarified, however, that he was not concluding that money laundering had taken place.
Remittances raise national security concerns
Batangas Rep. Gerville Luistro, the House of Representatives’ lead prosecutor in the impeachment case, previously called for a “full-blown national security investigation” into the remittances.

Three of the transfers had been reported by a bank as suspicious, Luistro said, adding that the transactions should be examined amid continuing tensions between the Philippines and China in the West Philippine Sea.

The National Security Council earlier said it would examine the reported foreign financial inflows and coordinate with intelligence and investigative agencies to determine whether they posed national security risks.
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. also said the allegations, if true, would constitute a national security issue and a threat to the country.
During the October 10 hearing, Cabrera claimed Cale 88 understated its revenue by an average of 51% a year, with P193.95 million in remittances coming from Chinese companies.
Hontiveros also flagged a Ukrainian company that sent money to Cale 88, saying her team found that the remitter matched a company under investigation in Kyiv for fraud and money laundering.
Senator-judge Joel Villanueva questioned Cale 88’s reported P150 million in sales in 2024 despite having only two employees on record.
The BIR is auditing whether Cale 88 underdeclared its sales, which could lead to deficiency taxes or a criminal case if tax evasion is proven.
The Senate impeachment trial will resume at 1 p.m. on Tuesday, October 13. — with a report from Cristina Chi

articles.title: Women's billion-dollar boom leaves players behind, says Fifpro
articles.summary: Women's football is on course to become a billion-dollar industry, but many professional players are still earning low wages, working on insecure contracts and experiencing rising psychological…

blocks.text: Women's football is on course to become a billion-dollar industry, but many professional players are still earning low wages, working on insecure contracts and experiencing rising psychological stress.
That is according to the findings of a new global survey of more than 800 footballers by the players' union Fifpro., external
Players were asked why they might leave football early. The report stated 59% cited financial reasons, while psychological stress was another factor identified by 46%.

Alex Culvin, head of women's football at Fifpro, said there was no single explanation for the increase. She pointed to growing public exposure, financial insecurity and inadequate support systems as possible contributing factors.
"Players are now very visible," she said.
"Players are not only expected to be visible, but are obligated to be visible because of the low income to subsidise the lack of solid income they receive."
While awareness of mental health issues has improved, Culvin explained many players felt they were being left to cope alone.
"Players also reported, whilst having a higher psychological stress, that they didn't have the support they needed in a mental health sense, either at the club or internationally," she said.
In total, the report shows 57% of women who responded to the survey struggled with their mental health and half of them were not provided with support by their clubs.
One of the report's most striking findings is how players view their own professional status.
Under Fifa's definition, a professional player has a written contract and is paid more than the expenses incurred playing.
In the survey, 62% of players described themselves as professional, 27% selected semi-professional and 12% chose amateur.
All players in the survey were playing for clubs in the top tier of their country, yet only 78% reported having a written contract and 82% said they were paid by their club.
However, just 57% said that payment was enough to cover the costs of playing football.
"Players who are professional but don't see or feel themselves as professional are not receiving the full benefits of being an employee," Culvin said.
The report also highlights the limits of salary growth. Although mean average monthly earnings have tripled since 2017 to $2,601 (£1,970), the median salary is just $1,669 (£1,250).

Average monthly pay varies considerably by region, from $6,450 (£4,886) in North America and $3,982 (£3,016) in central/Western Europe, to $878 (£664) in Eastern Europe and just $480 (£363) in Africa.
While salaries have risen sharply in leagues such as those in the USA and Mexico, average pay in 10 Eastern European countries remains below the national minimum wage.
Even in regions such as Western Europe and Asia/Oceania that span some bigger football markets, average pay is not significantly higher than national minimum wage levels.
Fifpro was unable to provide average salaries per league as the report focused on regions rather than individual countries.
Average contract lengths have also increased from about one year in 2017 to 19 months, but many players still face periods without guaranteed income.
"Only two-thirds of players are paid for the whole 12 months," said Culvin.
"There's a lot of players who are on seven-month contracts, nine-month contracts, which means that they've got to work to make up the rest of the calendar year."
She believes the rapid commercial growth of women's football has helped to obscure some of these realities.
Despite the rapid growth of England's Women's Super League, Fifpro says conditions at the top of the game could obscure the reality for many players elsewhere.
Culvin warned the economic boom in women's football could "mask some of the realities that players face and actually endure on a day-to-day basis".
The report also found that 24% of players had experienced late payments over the past two seasons, while 42% were not provided with a pension.
Culvin argues there is a growing disconnect between expectations and reality.
"I think there's a wake-up call needed for the ecosystem, that our players are suffering and that there is not the kind of wraparound support and accountability that's needed for players," she said.
However, not all trends were negative.
One significant improvement being felt in the game concerns parenthood.
In 2017, nearly half of respondents considering leaving the game early said wanting a family could drive them out of football.
That figure has now fallen to 19%, which Fifpro attributes in part to maternity regulations that were introduced by Fifa in 2021 and updated two years ago.
"What we've concluded, which I think is incredibly important, is that targeted regulatory intervention works - maternity regulations were introduced in 2021," said Culvin.

The report highlights a widening divide within the women's game. The sport's elite clubs and players have benefited from investment and visibility, yet much of the global workforce remains vulnerable.
"You've got an industry that's very focused on the top 5% of players," Culvin said.

"But then what you've got is the rest, which is 95% of the industry who are not paid on time, who have short contracts. They don't get paid for 12 months - they are in incredibly vulnerable and precarious environments."
Despite that, Fifpro insists the solution is not to slow down growth but to ensure that commercial success and player welfare develop together.
"There doesn't need to be a choice for those between commercial growth and player protection," said Culvin.
"Those two things need to go hand in hand and work in tandem."
Her conclusion is clear.

"What we're saying is enough is enough and the industry needs to react to the players' needs and centralise the players' voice, ensure that players have a seat at the table when decisions that affect them are being made about them."

articles.title: Row over Paris opera house ceiling reignites with lawsuit threat
articles.summary:
Descendant of 19-century artist demands removal of Marc Chagall’s 1960s canvases that cover original fresco

In 1962, the then French culture minister, André Malraux, reportedly bored by the…

blocks.text: In 1962, the then French culture minister, André Malraux, reportedly bored by the ballet he was watching at Paris’s opera house, raised his eyes to the classical ceiling and decided it needed a makeover.
In his ennui, Malraux thought his friend and artist Marc Chagall, sitting next to him at the Palais Garnier at the time, was the man for the job and commissioned him to make a new ceiling.

Over the next two years, Chagall worked in secret and for free to produce 24 enormous and colourful wedge-shaped canvasses, that were installed over the original 19th-century classical ceiling by the now forgotten artist Jules-Eugène Lenepveu.

blocks.caption: The Marc Chagall canvasses (above) were installed over the top of Jules-Eugène Lenepveu’s work. Photograph: Michal Sikorski/Alamy

blocks.text: Today, more than four decades after Chagall’s death, one of Lenepveu’s descendants is planning legal action to have the original ceiling uncovered and restored.

Arnaud Carayon says he has “asked nicely” for this to happen for three years, including writing two letters to France’s president, Emmanuel Macron. Now he has instructed a lawyer to take the fight to court.
“The Lenepveu ceiling is classified as a historic monument and yet it hasn’t been seen for 60 years and we have no idea what state it is in,” Carayon said.

blocks.caption: Jules-Eugène Lenepveu, who was chosen by Charles Garnier to paint the ceiling of the opera house. Photograph: Fernand Berthault

blocks.text: “Today, everyone has forgotten Lenepveu. Unfortunately, he was swept away by the wave of impressionism, but in his time he was really a star. More importantly, he was specifically chosen to decorate the opera ceiling by Charles Garnier, who designed everything in the opera house right down to the last door knob.
“But on a whim, Malraux decided he did not agree with Garnier’s choice.”
Garnier’s opera house was commissioned by Napoleon III and opened in January 1875 in the presence of European royals and political figures including the then lord mayor of London, Sir William Cotton.

Lenepveu, who was Garnier’s friend and artistic collaborator, produced a classical and allegorical work painted in oil directly on the copper plates of the opera house dome. The work, called The Muses and the Hours of Day and Night, and given historic listing in 1923, was considered perfectly in keeping with the ornate Second Empire style of Garnier’s palace.
Lenepveu, who went on to lead the French Academy in Rome, later produced a series of Joan of Arc frescoes in the Paris Panthéon, but his name is little known today.

Malraux is said to have wanted to give the fusty opera house a more modern, edgy feel. Chagall’s 24 cake-slice shaped canvasses were spliced together around the central chandelier covering 220 sq metres (2,368 sq ft) of the dome. The work is divided into separate colours: red, blue, green, yellow and white; and features dancers, angels, musicians and the names of composers.

blocks.caption: The foyer of the opera house, photographed after restoration work was completed in 2004. Photograph: Alfred/EPA

blocks.text: Even before Chagall’s work was installed, the row between traditionalists and modernists erupted and reached the other side of the Channel.

The Royal Institute of British Architects in London wrote to the French culture minister asking him to abandon plans to cover the original ceiling. “The unique character of this edifice [the opera house] is based on the fact that all its elements: architecture, paintings, sculptures and mosaics work together in harmony,” Riba wrote. Its plea was ignored.

The Palais Garnier will be closed for renovation between 2027-2032, and Carayon, the president of the Friends of Lenepveu Society, said he had written to Macron to suggest alternating the Lenepveu and Chagall ceilings after it reopens, with each being shown for a decade. He said the Élysée Palace replied only that the president was “particularly attentive” to the subject.

“From the beginning the Chagall ceiling was designed to be removable. It can be taken down without any damage. We thought the idea of alternating ceilings was very positive and promising, but it seems nobody has the guts to touch the Chagall ceiling,” Carayon said.

At a 2023-24 Chagall exhibition at the Pompidou Centre, the curator Anne Montfort-Tanguy, said: “The ceiling [of the opera house] is Chagall: it’s his autobiography, his vision of Paris. All the artists he loved are represented as well as what he considered the most important Paris monuments like the Eiffel Tower … It’s a moving, fluid almost cinematic work. The ceiling is a complete work of art.”

blocks.caption: The exterior of the Paris opera house, which was  commissioned by Napoleon III and opened in January 1875. Photograph: ALFRED/EPA

blocks.text: “It was Chagall’s gift to the country that welcomed him; a homage to France and to Paris,” Montfort-Tanguy added.

Alexander Neef, the director of the Paris Opera, told Le Monde: “The debate over the Chagall ceiling has gone on for more than 60 years. The Lenepveu ceiling has been listed as a historic monument since 1923 so its heritage value is recognised. That his [Lenepveu’s] descendants wish to defend his memory is legitimate.”

articles.title: Republican US senator facing re-election settles six-year bakery debt
articles.summary:
Roger Marshall says he has ‘no idea how this happened’ and repaid bill double for 2020 election watch party treats

The

blocks.text: The Republican US senator Roger Marshall says he has finally paid off a bakery debt – after six years and repeated collection attempts reported by a Kansas business that had supplied a large order of treats for a 2020 election watch party.

“We have absolutely no idea how this happened”, the Kansas senator wrote in a social media post containing a screenshot of the payment on a $678.75 invoice from Holly’s Sweet Treats as well as his $1,300 payment. “And we have repaid the bill … double.”

Word of Marshall’s cookie debt became widely known after an 8 October social media post from Holly Thomas, a baker from Hutchinson, Kansas, which began: “Do you know why I will never vote for Roger Marshall?”

The Holly’s Sweet Treats proprietor recounted how Marshall’s campaign had “ordered cookies and treats from my bakery” for a 2020 primary election watch party that preceded his winning his first six-year Senate term.
“For nearly a year,” the post continued, “I made repeated attempts to collect payment, reaching out by phone and email. I never received a return phone call, and the invoice was never paid.”
Thomas said that unpaid invoice was particularly challenging because it was during the Covid-19 pandemic, “when small businesses everywhere were struggling just to keep their doors open”.
“Every single dollar mattered,” Thomas wrote. “Those cookies and treats cost money to make, employees’ time to prepare, and resources that my little business couldn’t afford to give away.”

blocks.caption: Roger Marshall and his wife, Laina, thank supporters for a win at an election watch party in Topeka, Kansas, on 3 November 2020. Photograph: Orlin Wagner/AP

blocks.text: Thomas concluded: “Six years later, I haven’t forgotten. This isn’t about political parties or policy disagreements. It’s about my personal experience as a small business owner and the importance of honoring financial commitments.
“That experience is why Roger Marshall will never get my vote.”
Thomas’s post achieved internet virality and unsurprisingly caught the attention of Marshall’s camp.

By Saturday, Marshall had published his own social media post addressing Thomas’s statement, saying on X: “As some folks may have seen, there was a post on social media regarding an unpaid 2020 cookie bill.

“We have absolutely no idea how this happened, but rest assured as soon as it became known to us, we immediately attempted to contact the business in order to apologize, and we have repaid the bill from 2020, double.”

Marshall’s post – along with the picture of the paid invoice to Holly’s Sweet Treats – quickly drew a community note from X users aiming to provide what the platform characterized as additional context.
“Multiple attempts to get paid were ignored,” the community note said, linking to Thomas’s Facebook post.
Many users gave Marshall what they considered his just desserts in the form of harsh comments, with one commenter saying: “You got caught, and that’s the only reason you paid.”
Others calculated that he actually owed Thomas more than $1,400 at 18% simple annual interest for six years. And one noted that $678.75 doubled is $1,357.50 – not $1,300.
Thomas on Saturday published another Facebook post that acknowledged Marshall’s having “paid his bill”.
“Better later than never, right?” Thomas wrote. “Six years later, I guess we can finally mark that invoice PAID!”
Marshall’s response to Thomas’ publicizing his late payment unfolded in a political climate which has the Democrats favored to win control of the US House during the 3 November midterms.

Polls more recently have shown that the Democrats also have a relatively viable chance to win US Senate seats in states that traditionally elect Republicans and possibly gain a majority in that chamber, too – given Donald Trump’s unpopularity amid high living costs and the war in Iran that the president helped start alongside Israel.

Marshall’s announcement about paying Thomas also arrived after the Cook Political Report amended its prediction for his November re-election run against Democratic challenger Adam Hamilton from leaning in the Republican’s favor to being considered a toss-up.

The announcement from Marshall – a physician – about the tardily settled bill also came after the New York Times reported in September that his obstetrics-gynecology practice had sued hundreds of patients over the years in connection with unpaid medical bills, including for as little as $101.

articles.title: News Reflection: Alan Peter Cayetano doesn’t spread gossip

blocks.text: The self-confessed 'ambassador of Christ' knows his credibility is on the line
When it comes to his credibility, Senator Alan Peter Cayetano makes no compromise. He says his mother and father taught him never to spread gossip, because his reputation would be on the line.
Cayetano, who once said he was an “ambassador of Christ,” questions the Anti-Money Laundering Council’s reference to news reports in its inquiry into Vice President Sara Duterte’s money trail.

As a senator-judge in Duterte’s impeachment trial, Cayetano knows only A-1 information deserves airtime before the court. Just like his supposition that the Philippines has become comparable to Singapore when it comes to the safety of its streets, and his proposal to grant every Filipino family P10,000 as ayuda in recovering from the pandemic.

articles.title: 2,000 protesters march to Senate, demand Sara Duterte's conviction
articles.summary: Akbayan Partylist and several groups marched to the Senate in Pasay City on Monday, calling for the conviction of Vice President Sara Duterte as the impeachment court tackled Article 2 of the…

blocks.text: Published October 12, 2026 5:57pm

Akbayan Partylist and several groups marched to the Senate in Pasay City on Monday, calling for the conviction of Vice President Sara Duterte as the impeachment court tackled Article 2 of the Articles of Impeachment concerning her alleged unexplained wealth.

More than 2,000 individuals participated in the protest, including Fr. Robert Reyes of the Clergy for Good Governance, Kiko Aquino Dee of Tindig Pilipinas, Magdalo, Mamamayang Liberal, the August Twenty One Movement (ATOM), the Student Council Alliance of the Philippines (SCAP), Everywoman, Kilos Maralita, Partido Manggagawa, Sentro Labor Center, Kalipunan and Akbayan Youth.

“Tapos na ang boksing. Hindi na maiiwasan pa ni Sara ang kaliwa’t kanang bigwas ng katotohanan. Panahon para sa Senado na i-knockout na sa pwesto ang Bise Presidente, na isa sa lantarang simbolo hindi lamang ng katiwalian kundi maging ng kataksilan sa bayan,” Akbayan President Rafaela David said.

(The fight is over. Sara can no longer avoid the relentless blows of truth from all sides. It is time for the Senate to knock the Vice President out of office, as she is one of the blatant symbols not only of corruption but also of betrayal of the nation.)

The Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) confirmed that a company linked to the Vice President and her husband, Atty Man Carpio, received P319 million from China and Hong Kong, of which P315.93 million came from Mainland China, while P3.39 million was from the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of China.
Transaction records from AMLC also showed that an estimated P4.4 billion went in and out of Carpio’s accounts from 2007 to 2025.

Protesters also questioned the loyalty of the Vice President and her family to the country amid China’s continuing aggression in the West Philippine Sea and harassment of Filipino fisherfolk and frontliners, following the revelations about the couple’s alleged spending and transactions.

“Ninanakawan na nga tayo, pinagtatrayduran pa! Ang bansang kanilang pinagnakawan ay bansang kanila ring binenta sa dayuhan. Sa kanilang kawalan ng hiya, hindi na lang sila akusadong plunderer, china-funded traitor pa!” David said.

(We are being robbed and betrayed at the same time! The country they have stolen from is the same country they have sold out to foreigners. With their shamelessness, they are not just accused of plunder but also of being China-funded traitors!)
In response to the allegation about their ties with China, Duterte questioned the prosecution and asked if doing business with China is prohibited.

"So ano ba talaga? Bawal ba talaga amg negosyo with China kasi it is a national security risk. Parang nakakahiya na nga yung drug haul na papuntang Pilipinas galing Laos and Thailand tapos eto pa tayo na nagsasabing na naku it’s a national security risk na mag negosyo with China. Nagiging troublemaker of Southeast Asia tayo," Duterte said.

(So what is it, then? Is doing business with China really prohibited because it poses a national security risk? It’s already embarrassing that we have a drug shipment bound for the Philippines from Laos and Thailand, and now we’re saying that doing business with China is a national security risk. We’re becoming the troublemaker of Southeast Asia.) —Mariel Celine Serquiña/RF, GMA News

articles.summary: The Northeasterly windflow is expected to affect extreme Northern Luzon, while the easterlies will prevail over Luzon and the eastern section of Visayas on October 13, 2026, the state weather bureau…

blocks.text: Published October 12, 2026 5:55pm

The Northeasterly windflow is expected to affect extreme Northern Luzon, while the easterlies will prevail over Luzon and the eastern section of Visayas on October 13, 2026, the state weather bureau PAGASA said Monday.
In its 4 p.m. bulletin, the bureau said the northeasterly windflow is forecast to bring partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated light rains over Batanes and the Babuyan Islands.
The easterlies are expected to bring cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms over the Bicol Region, Eastern Visayas, Aurora, and Quezon.

Meanwhile, partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rainshowers or thunderstorms are forecast over Metro Manila, Ilocos Region, Cordillera Administrative Region, Occidental Mindoro, Oriental Mindoro, Marinduque, Romblon, and the rest of Cagayan Valley, Central Luzon, and CALABARZON due to the Easterlies.
In the rest of the country, partly cloudy to cloudy skies with isolated rain showers or thunderstorms are likewise expected, brought by localized thunderstorms.

As of 3 p.m., a tropical depression was located outside the Philippine area of responsibility, 2,970 kilometers east of Central Luzon, with maximum sustained winds of 45 kmh and gusts of up to 55 kmh.
Moderate winds and coastal waters are expected in Northern Luzon, Central Luzon, and the eastern sections of Southern Luzon and Visayas. Waves are expected to run from 1.5 meters to 2.5 meters.
Light to moderate winds and slight to moderate coastal waters are expected in the rest of the country, with waves running from 0.6 meters to 1.8 meters.

At the PAGASA Science Garden weather station in Diliman, Quezon City, the highest temperature recorded on Monday reached 31.5 degrees Celsius at 2 p.m., while the lowest temperature was logged at 24.5 degrees Celsius at 4:00 a.m.
Sunrise in Metro Manila on Tuesday is at 5:47 a.m. —Lyjah Tiffany Bonzo/LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Nobel Prize in Economics goes to pair of US economists
articles.summary: The pair got the Nobel for developing economic models that help governments and central banks respond more effectively to booms and recessions.

image.caption: Hall is affiliated with Stanford University in California, and Woodford with Columbia University in New YorkImage: Jonathan Nackstrand/AFP

blocks.text: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences was awarded to Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford, the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences in Stockholm announced on Monday.

The pair got the Nobel for their work in microeconomic foundations of stabilization policy, allowing for the development of economic models that help governments and central banks respond more effectively to booms and recessions.
Hall is affiliated with Stanford University in California, and Woodford with Columbia University in New York.
"It's a tremendous honor, it's a surprise," Woodford said, addressing the committee by phone from New York on Monday.
Why did Hall and Woodford win the Nobel Prize?
The pair of US scientists were awarded for looking toward microeconomic indicators to inform macroeconomic stabilization policies.
They have based their economic models on a microeconomic foundation, breaking with the longstanding Keynesian models, developed by economist John Maynard Keynes almost a century ago.
The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences argued that decades of applying the Keynesian models showed their limitations – including in failing to curb unemployment and instead raise inflation.
Inflation: A global threat

"The West experienced a decade of low growth, high unemployment and high inflation. Many people believed that stabilization policy had done more harm than good and that it should be retired," the academy said in its press release.
Hall and Woodford's model instead demonstrated how the total mass of individual households and businesses affect the economy through their actions.

"The Laureates' work has provided us with a stable theoretical foundation for the models that are now used by central banks and governments around the world. With them, we are better equipped to deal with shocks in the economy, such as energy crises or sudden changes in how much households consume," said John Hassler, Chair of the Committee for the Prize in Economic Sciences.
What else to know about the Nobel Economics prize?
The economics prize is formally known as the Bank of Sweden Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel.

Last year's prize was awarded to three business innovation researchers who explained how new products and inventions promote economic growth and human welfare, even as they leave older companies behind.
The Sveriges Riksbank established it in 1968 as a memorial to Nobel, the 19th-century Swedish businessman and chemist who invented dynamite and established the five Nobel Prizes.
Since the economics prize was not one of the five original Nobel Prizes established by Nobel in his will, some argue that it is not technically not a Nobel Prize.
Nevertheless, it is always presented together with the others on December 10, the anniversary of Nobel's death in 1896.
Nobel honors were announced last week in medicine, physics, chemistry, literature and peace.
This year's prize money is 12 million Swedish kronor (about $1.2 million or €1.07 million), whether for an individual, small group of laureates or organization.

articles.title: French centre left must wage ‘existential battle’ to prevent far right winning presidency
articles.summary:
French MEP Raphaël Glucksmann issues call after becoming the social democrat candidate for 2027 presidential run

The European lawmaker Raphaël Glucksmann has urged the French centre left to…

blocks.text: The European lawmaker Raphaël Glucksmann has urged the French centre left to wage an “existential battle” to prevent Marine Le Pen’s far right winning the 2027 presidential election after he was chosen as the social democrat candidate for the presidency.

“We’ve got to rid our hearts of the spirit of defeat,” Glucksmann, the founder of the small party Place Publique, said on Monday morning after his decisive win in a centre-left primary race held by the Socialist party.

In his first interview since being designated a presidential candidate on Sunday night, Glucksmann told France Inter radio that the country was living in a “historic moment”, with the far right at the gates of power. He said the 2027 presidential election campaign would be brutal and “like no other we have ever experienced”. He said it would be unbearable to have a centre left “that doesn’t believe in victory”, adding that he could restore a “pride in social democracy”.

At present the centre left sits substantially behind the far right in the polls and also trails the radical left politician Jean-Luc Mélenchon, who is polling high but with whom Glucksmann refuses to work.

Glucksmann, 46, an essayist and intellectual who argues he is very different to career politicians, is staunchly pro-Europe and pro-Ukraine. His candidacy marks the first time the Socialist party will not have its own presidential candidate since the party was founded in 1969. The party suffered two crushing defeats in the last two presidential elections.

Glucksmann has been a member of the European parliament since 2019. He strikes a more reformist and centrist tone than the Socialist party, but has cooperated with it in the past, presenting joint electoral lists. He has made no secret of his presidential ambitions but needed the Socialist party machine behind him for his campaign.
Glucksman is polling at between 9% and 14%, well behind the frontrunner, Le Pen. He also trails the centre-right contender Édouard Philippe, who served as prime minister under Emmanuel Macron.
Crucially, he is also behind Mélenchon, whose party, La France Insoumise, boycotted the Socialist primary and has presented itself as the biggest force in a divided left.

Glucksmann is tasked with regaining centre-left voters who jumped ship to support Macron, though his critics on the left accuse him of being too centrist. He said the French president, who is standing down next spring, “wasted 10 years” failing to act on the climate emergency.

Glucksmann is known for being a campaigner on international issues. He took part in documentary work to raise awareness of the aftermath of genocide in Rwanda and is a former adviser to the anti-Moscow former Georgian president Mikheil Saakashvili.

Glucksmann, who has been accused by opponents of being too much of a Paris intellectual, said he “lost sleep at night” worrying about how the social-democratic left had lost the working class in France. He said the centre left needed to regain “a form of radicality that we lost” and the focus of this would be environmental policy.
He told the daily Libération he made no apology for being an intellectual and would use his background to “better explain the moment we’re living in” rather than relying on “slogans”.
Glucksmann’s partner, Léa Salamé, is the star presenter of the French public broadcaster’s flagship evening news programme. She has stepped down from presenting the news while he runs for president.

articles.title: CA dismisses Alice Guo's motion for release from detention
articles.summary: The Court of Appeals (CA) has denied the appeal of dismissed Bamban, Tarlac Mayor Alice Guo against her detention.

blocks.text: Published October 12, 2026 5:37pm
The Court of Appeals (CA) has denied the appeal of dismissed Bamban, Tarlac Mayor Alice Guo against her detention.

In an 8-page resolution promulgated on October 5, the former 1st Division dismissed the motion for reconsideration filed by Guo against the court’s ruling that dismissed her petition for habeas corpus.
“Without any new cogent or plausible justification raised in the present Motion, the Court sees no reason to reverse its Resolution,” it said.
Guo had challenged the authority of the Bureau of Immigration (BI).
However, the CA said that it is a “simple and inescapable fact” that Guo is not under the BI but is under the Correctional Institution for Women since December 2025.

“She is detained not by virtue of any warrant or order by the BI, but by the RTC’s Joint Decision. There is neither allegation nor showing that such detention violated petitioner’s constitutional rights to speedy trial and to liberty,” it said.
“In fact, there is absolutely no proof that the RTC’s Joint Decision was unlawful, or that the court a quo lacked jurisdiction,” it added.
Guo has been sentenced to life imprisonment over qualified human trafficking. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: [Vantage Point] DBP’s bad loans: The failures behind the billions
articles.summary: The Commission on Audit has uncovered serious deficiencies in state-owned DBP's lending practices, credit safeguards, and recovery procedures

items: The Commission on Audit (COA) has identified significant deficiencies in the Development Bank of the Philippines' (DBP) lending practices, leading to a rise in non-performing loans from P42.68 billion in 2024 to P46.50 billion in 2025, and a nearly 43% drop in net income.

COA's audit revealed systemic failures in loan administration, including inadequate collateral verification and sluggish recovery measures, which have raised concerns about DBP's financial resilience and accountability.

The ICONS program, intended to support government infrastructure projects, has become a financial liability with a significant portion of its loans overdue, highlighting mismanagement and the need for urgent reforms within DBP.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

Following Vantage Point’s exposé earlier this year on the Development Bank of the Philippines’ P36.21-billion non-performing loan portfolio, the Commission on Audit (COA) has uncovered serious deficiencies in the state-owned bank’s lending practices, credit safeguards and recovery procedures. With gross bad loans swelling to P46.50 billion and net income plunging by nearly 43%, COA’s 2025 audit reveals how weaknesses in credit administration, delayed collections and questionable loan-loss estimates have placed mounting pressure on DBP’s profitability, financial resilience and stewardship of public funds.

When Vantage Point exposed the Development Bank of the Philippines’ (DBP) P36.21-billion non-performing loan portfolio last January, the underlying concern extended far beyond the identities of delinquent borrowers.

The fundamental question was how a government-owned development institution could amass billions in troubled loans without triggering immediate alarms regarding its credit discipline, financial resilience, and internal accountability.

Now, the Commission on Audit’s (COA) newly obtained 2025 Annual Audit Report provides disturbing answers to those exact concerns. According to the government’s own auditors, the bank suffers from documented deficiencies in loan releases, inadequate collateral verification, sluggish recovery measures, and an outdated expected-credit-loss model.

The financial consequences of these operational shortcomings are unmistakable. DBP’s parent-bank gross non-performing loans escalated significantly, rising from P42.68 billion in 2024 to P46.50 billion in 2025.

To absorb this, its allowance against non-performing loans jumped from P23.03 billion to P33.49 billion. Consequently, the bank’s net income plunged by 42.9%, dropping from P7.30 billion to P4.17 billion. Put simply, while DBP technically remained profitable, its rapidly deteriorating credit quality took a heavy toll on its overall earnings.

The initial investigation scrutinized P36,208,917,505.63 in non-performing exposures across 442 businesses and individual borrowers. Among the largest exposures were Premium Megastructures Inc. with P3.4 billion, Manuel and Theresa Chua with P3.31 billion, Dennis Uy‘s Phoenix Petroleum Philippines Inc. with P2.93 billion, and Megaship Builders Inc. with P2.4 billion. Combined, these four accounts represented approximately one-third of the entire troubled portfolio examined.

blocks.caption: [Vantage Point] DBP’s ₱36.2-B NPL exposure emerges as a state-level credit risk

blocks.text: While COA’s audit anonymized its sampled borrowers—meaning no direct documentary link has been formally established between these specific named accounts and the latest audit cases—the newly documented systemic failures substantially confirm our January exposé. The core issue was whether DBP’s internal systems for evaluating, monitoring, and recovering funds were robust enough to safeguard the public interest.

This systemic vulnerability is most vividly illustrated by COA’s examination of the Infrastructure Contractor Support (ICONS) program. Launched in 2017 to finance contractors for the government’s Build, Build, Build initiative, the program devolved into a financial liability.

blocks.caption: Image from DBP Development Banker, April-June 2018 issue

blocks.text: By December 31, 2025, ICONS carried P6.67 billion in outstanding loans. Alarmingly, P4.09 billion—or approximately 61.4% of that portfolio—was already past due. For every P10 outstanding, more than P6 was overdue, representing a troubling outcome for a program supposedly anchored by secure government infrastructure contracts.

COA’s deep dive into specific loans reveals exactly how these funds were mismanaged. Auditors examined a P300-million corporate loan approved in August 2019, where funds were released against assigned receivables from government projects.

However, releases bypassed progress-based disbursement rules, and actual project accomplishments were never properly verified before the capital was deployed. The borrower ceased payments in June 2020, and several of the underlying projects were eventually terminated for delays.

More than five years after default, the P300-million principal remains unpaid, forcing DBP to provide a 100% allowance against the exposure. Similarly, a P490.46-million loan account revealed that the underlying security projects were completed between 2017 and 2021, yet the debt remained unsettled. Auditors discovered the borrower had aggressively subcontracted the work, retaining an actual economic interest of only 3.5%, raising questions about how DBP assessed the borrower’s repayment cash flows.

Recovery efforts were equally flawed. One P97.24-million loan defaulted in June 2021, yet the first recorded demand notice was not issued until July 2025 after passing through six different account officers, undermining accountability. Another P82.21-million exposure languished waiting for foreclosure proceedings simply because the lending center lacked a full-time lawyer.

Most concerning is that DBP’s board was aware of these mounting issues. Under Resolution No. 0044, dated January 19, 2022, the board instructed units to investigate the 20 largest non-performing loans. Yet, it took more than four years for the board to officially terminate the ICONS program on June 3, 2026. COA has now recommended investigating potential negligence among officers, prompting DBP’s Management Committee to direct its Legal Services Group to conduct an inquiry.

Furthermore, COA discovered that DBP’s P49.88-billion allowance for credit losses relied on an expected-credit-loss model that was not properly recalibrated to current observable data, violating Philippine Financial Reporting Standard 9.
Expected-credit-loss models dictate how much a bank must recognize today against loans that may not be recovered tomorrow, relying heavily on probabilities of default and collateral values.

When uncalibrated, the reported allowances may fail to reflect prevailing risks. Consequently, auditors stated that the faithful representation of the bank’s P491.42-billion net loans balance and P12.52-billion impairment expense could not be established.

While DBP’s gross loan portfolio remained static at roughly P536.69 billion, its allowance surged by P11.78 billion. Concurrently, the appraised value of collateral held against impaired loans plummeted by P39.62 billion, dropping from P104.17 billion in 2024 to just P64.55 billion in 2025.

Although DBP maintains financial soundness with an 11.22% capital adequacy ratio and an unmodified audit opinion, regulatory capital compliance does not eliminate the necessity to fix costly internal control weaknesses.
The fact that 25 of COA’s 38 previous audit recommendations remained unimplemented by December 2025 underscores a sluggish approach to structural reform.

These findings firmly vindicate the demand for a transparent, independent asset-quality review and a serious reconsideration of merging DBP with LandBank to consolidate risk oversight. Public confidence in a development institution must be earned through disciplined lending, transparent accounting, and decisive accountability when financial safeguards inevitably fail. – Rappler.com

Documentary basis: DBP’s 2025 COA Annual Audit Report, particularly printed pages 6, 50–57, 76–79, 91–94, 102–103 and 158–164. The named borrower exposures derive from Vantage Point’s earlier investigation, not from COA’s anonymized ICONS findings. The audit’s unmodified opinion and unresolved recommendations are recorded in its executive summary.
