articles.title: Erice 'ashamed' that 2027 national budget has another large public works allocation
articles.summary: Caloocan Rep. Edgar Erice expressed embarrassment over the 2027 national budget that the House passed on second reading, citing another large allocation for public works projects.

blocks.text: Caloocan 2nd District Representative Edgar Erice expressed embarrassment over the 2027 national budget that the lower chamber recently passed on second reading, citing another large allocation for public works projects.
The House of Representatives passed on second reading Thursday the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget, with the third and final reading scheduled for today, Monday.
“Sabi nung 2025 SONA ni Pangulong Marcos, mahiya naman kayo. Itong ipinasa namin na second reading, ako, ang reaction ko diyan, nahiya ako. Nakakahiya,” Erice said on Unang Hirit on Monday.
(In President Marcos’s 2025 SONA, he said, ‘You should be ashamed.’ Looking at what we passed on second reading, my reaction was that I felt ashamed. It is shameful.)

According to Erice, one of the reasons why he could not vote in favor of the budget was the failure to learn from yet another massive allocation for public works—funds that had already been removed for this year.

“‘Yung 2025 budget, tinanggalan ’yung mga flagship projects, inilagay sa Public Works. Ngayon, ganito rin, P11 billion yung inilagay muli sa Public Works. Bukod doon, ‘yung mismong public works project ay hinati-hati at binago. May kinaltasan, may dinagdagan,” Erice said.

(In the 2025 budget, funds were stripped from flagship projects and reallocated to Public Works. Now, the same thing is happening, with P11 billion realigned to Public Works once again. Beyond that, the public works projects themselves were split up and modified—some were reduced, while others were increased.)

He added that lawmakers like him who voted to abstain or voted against the impeachment of Vice President Duterte allegedly suffered fund cuts, whereas allies and prosecutors received additional funding.

Erice noted that under the proposed 2027 national budget, Bulacan received additional funds, bringing the entire province's share to around P11 billion, whereas his district was allotted only P269 million for public works.
The congressman remarked that his fellow lawmakers have failed to learn, describing them as people who “ayaw mabulunan.”
Presidential pork?

Erice raised again his criticism that the Local Government Support Fund (LGSF) serves as a “presidential pork barrel,” noting that its initial P58.53-billion allocation in the national budget has now ballooned to around P62 billion due to additional funding.
The congressman also flagged the overly broad scope allowed for the funds, which could be spent on any project and allocated to any local government unit.
Erice urged the government to establish clear parameters and a concrete basis for how the LGSF should be spent.

“Inilabas ko ‘yan during the budget deliberations that the government spend P22 B distributed to local governments. At ang pinakamasama, kung sino yung mga mayayaman na probinsya, like Quezon City, na mga city, sila pa 'yung pinakamalalaking allocation,” Erice said.

(I raised that during the budget deliberations—that the government spent P22 billion distributed to local governments. What makes it worse is that the wealthiest provinces and cities, like Quezon City, received the largest allocations.)
“Anong basis? ‘Di ba dapat support fund sa local government? Kung sino ‘yung pinakamangangailangan, kung sino ‘yung mga naghihirap? Eh ‘yung Batanes, zero. Maguindanao, zero. Aurora, zero,” he added.
(What is the basis? Isn't it supposed to be a support fund for local government units—for those who are most in need and struggling? Yet Batanes got zero, Maguindanao got zero, and Aurora got zero.)

Erice said he might clarify the matter before the Supreme Court if the P62-billion allocation and its “anything under the sun” spending guidelines remain in the 2027 national budget when signed into law.
Malacañang has defended the LGSF, and said that describing the fund as a presidential pork barrel was merely “pang-intriga” (for intrigue).
Transparency
Amid concerns over the rapid pace of deliberations on the national budget in the lower chamber, Erice said that he had no objection to the speed itself.

However, he urged full transparency in the budget process, alleging that the small committee reemerged during the Budget Amendments and Review Subcommittee (BARC) deliberation, where potential modifications to the budget were made.

“Ang problema, during the BARC, yung small committee bumalik na naman. Doon na naman pinagbabago yung mga budget at inilagay doon sa NEP, National Expenditure Program. May mga project na doon na pinag-aralan. ‘Yun tinanggal,” Erice alleged.

(The problem is that during the BARC, the small committee was brought back once again. That is where they modified the budget and inserted changes into the NEP, removing projects that had already been thoroughly studied.)
“Tapos hindi mo alam kung saan kumuha ng mga proyekto, kung saan kamay ng demonyo kinuha ‘yun at sinaksak doon sa budget. ‘Yan ‘yung isang problema,” he added.
(Then you no longer know where these new projects came from—out of nowhere, they were suddenly injected into the budget. That is the problem.)
Erice claimed there is a reluctance to be transparent regarding the budget process, particularly regarding where the additional P5-billion budget for the House of Representatives will go.

“Yung pondo ng ano, ng bilyong-bilyon na pondo ng House of Representatives, dinagdagan pa ng P5 billion. Eh, ang dami na namin savings. Eh, saan mapupunta 'yun? At hindi ayaw sabihin kung paano hinahati-hati ‘yun,” the congressman said.

(The billions of pesos in funding for the House of Representatives was increased by another P5 billion. We already have substantial savings. So where will that go? And they refuse to disclose how it is being divided.)

Erice urged transparency about how much each lawmaker receives, emphasizing that funds ought to be distributed in an equitable manner based on committee assignments and leadership positions. — BM, GMA News

articles.title: Germany's women: Ena Mahmutovic makes her case to become Germany's next No.1 goalkeeper
articles.summary: Germany's win against Australia saw Ena Mahmutovic excel in goal. The 22-year-old Bayern Munich goalkeeper is considered the successor to Ann-Katrin Berger and is making a name for herself.

image.caption: Ena Mahmutovic impressed in Germany's game against AustraliaImage: Hansjürgen Britsch/Baumann/picture alliance

blocks.text: With determination, pace, and four beautifully crafted goals, Germany's women won its friendly against Australia, thrilling not only the fans but also head coach Christian Wück.

"You can see how fired up the girls are, how well they're already playing together, and that we have an incredible amount of talent on the field and on the bench," said a delighted Wück after his team's well-deserved 4-2 victory.

Since there were several notable absences, including captain Giulia Gwinn and top scorer Lea Schüller, others had to step up and fill the gaps. And they did so with flying colors. Melissa Kössler made a strong case for herself as a striker by scoring her first two international goals. Center back Camilla Küver and Sjoeke Nüsken were also on the scoresheet.
Mahmutovic seizes her chance in goal

Much like it was with the men's team during Jürgen Klopp's first international break as Germany head coach, the question as to who will emerge as the next number one goalkeeper for the women was also a hot topic.

blocks.caption: The understudy and the current No.1: Ena Mahmutovic and Ann-Katrin BergerImage: Madeleine Fantini/HMB Media/picture alliance

blocks.text: The difference is that unlike Manuel Neuer, who has retired from international football, Ann-Katrin Berger is sticking around for at least one more tournament cycle.

However, with just three matches to go before the start of the playoffs in the National Women's Soccer League (NWSL), where she plays for Gotham FC, Berger is giving these two Germany friendlies a miss.
Parallels to men's goalkeeping situation
This means 22-year-old Bayern Munich goalkeeper Ena Mahmutovic, who is seen as a potential successor to Berger, took her her chance.

"Ena deserves to play the next match," Wück said ahead of the game. "We must not forget that she already kept a clean sheet in Slovenia (Germany's last World Cup qualifier). And I hope she can repeat that tomorrow."

Some will draw parallels to Jonas Urbig, who many see as a future number one for Germany's men. Both he and Mahmutovic were born in 2003 in the western state of North Rhine-Westphalia, and both are seen as up-and-coming stars for their club and country.

blocks.caption: Manuel Neuer remains the first choice at Bayern, while Jonas  Urbig looks set to become Germany's No. 1Image: Frank Hoermann/SvenSimon/picture alliance

blocks.text: The difference is that while Urbig remains an understudy to Neuer at Bayern, Mahmutovic is already the first-choice keeper at her club, having won the starting job over Maria Luisa Grohs prior to the start of the season.
For Germany, though, Mahmutovic still has to bide her time, while there are already strong indications that Klopp intends to make Urbig his number one.
'The future of the national team'
"I'm obviously delighted," Mahmutovic said ahead of the games.
"It's always something special, of course – especially playing against a team from another continent. I think testing ourselves against them is very helpful as we look ahead to the World Cup."
Bayern director Bianca Rech recently described Mahmutovic as "the future of the national team," calling on Wück not only to give her a callup, but also regular playing time.
Wück still sees Berger as slightly better than Mahmutovic, but he is also full of praise for the young keeper.
"Ena's performances have been very good," he said. "She will get her playing time."

blocks.caption: When Ena Mahmutovic lost control of the ball after a backpass, Italy's Sofia Cantore took full advantageImage: David Inderlied/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Costly mistake in Germany debut

The match against Slovenia was just Mahmutovic's second appearances for Germany. Her first, which came almost two years ago, was memorable for the wrong reason. In the dying minutes of a friendly in December 2024, she lost control of the ball after a back pass, allowing an Italian forward to score the winner in a 2-1 defeat for Germany. Still, Mahmutovic was included in Germany's squad for the 2025 Euros.
Had it been up to her father – who is from Montenegro – Mahmutovic would never have become a goalkeeper.
"He still says I would have been better as an outfield player because I'm good with both feet," she said.
Unusual Bundesliga debut

That's a quality that evidently wasn't lost on Thomas Gerstner, when her coach at her then-club Duisburg, gave her her Women's Bundesliga debut in May 2020. With the team coping with several absences, the then-16-year-old, who had been on the bench as backup goalkeeper, came on as an outfield player.
"The coach brought me on during stoppage time," Mahmutovic recalled. "I got to make two sprints – that was my debut."
That, however, was a one-off, and nobody questions Mahmutovic's strengths as a goalkeeper.
"She is one of the most talented goalkeepers in the world," said Bayern coach Jose Barcala, noting that she is the kind of player who can decide a match.
Mahmutovic will be hoping she gets many more opportunities to do just that for Germany.
This article was originally published in German.
This article was updated on October 12 after Germany's friendly against Australia.

articles.title: Witness: Sara Duterte, husband's financial records show 'symptoms of money laundering'
articles.summary: The financial transactions of Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio, show "symptoms of money laundering," a certified public accountant and lawyer said Monday.

blocks.text: The financial transactions of Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio, show "symptoms of money laundering," a certified public accountant and lawyer said Monday.
Prosecution witness Alexander Cabrera, a financial analyst, testified on Day 38 of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

Cabrera, who reviewed the bank transactions, bank records, tax records, and corporate records involving the Vice President and her husband, cited P41 million and P55 million unused manager's checks under the joint account of the Vice President and her father, former President Rodrigo Duterte.
The P41 million was eventually used as a payout to Mr. Duterte and P16 million to businessman Sammy Uy. On the same day, Carpio also made a P41 million over-the-counter withdrawal.

“Ito po yung mga telltale signs na may fraudulent reporting po na nangyayari. Actually, first time ko po nakakita nung ganun po, yung managers check po na labas-pasok po. Pero totoo naman po yung sinabi ng defense. Wala pong pirma si VP Sara doon sa managers’ check. Pero yung time deposit po na nakapangalan po sa kanya pero wala po siyang pirma, nawala po yung interest doon eh,” Cabrera said during the questioning of Senator-judge Risa Hontiveros.

(There are telltale signs of fraudulent reporting. Manager's checks coming in and out. The Vice President's signature was not on the manager's'check, but the time deposit under her name lost interest because it was made a manager's check.)

Marwin Galvez, division head for central Manila branches of Bank of the Philippine Islands (BPI), earlier testified that an amount in a manager’s check is not reflected on the ending balance of the account holder.

“Kahit sabihin po nating hindi nakapangalan kay VP Sara, may accountability naman po siya sa bank account because of and/or po yun. Nawala po ‘yung interest doon sa time deposit dahil ginawa pong managers’ check. So to give up interest on a large amount like that doesn't really make any business sense. Iyon po ang point namin; it is a concealment method. Sintomas po ‘yun ng money laundering,” Cabrera added.

(Even if we say that the account was not in Vice President Sara Duterte’s name, she still had accountability for it because it was an ‘and/or’ account. The time deposit also stopped earning interest when it was converted into a manager’s check. Giving up the interest on such a large amount does not make business sense. That is our point: it was a method of concealment and a symptom of money laundering.)
Cabrera said that while the Vice President did not sign the manager’s checks, the behavior of the account stays.

“I am not saying that there is money laundering. I am just saying there are symptoms. Pag ang pera po ay pumasok sa company, lumabas po the same day o lumabas po the following day, ang ibig sabihin po noon it didn't add any value to the company,” Cabrera added.
(When money enters a company and comes out the same day or the following day, it does not add any value to the company.)
GMA News Online reached out to Sara Duterte's spokesman, Paolo Panelo, for comment and will update this post once it is available.
Cabrera also flagged the P41 million withdrawal over the counter of Carpio, dated August 6, 2024.

This P41 million is broken down into P23 million from BDO Unibank Inc. (BDO) and P18 million from Philippine National Bank (PNB), as testified by Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura of the Anti-Money Laundering Council.

“P41 million in cash, kailangan niyo po siyempre ng bag po doon. Parang may hinahabol po kasi, lahat po ginawa within the hour po. Pwede rin po yung i-cheke, o i-manager’s check at i-deposit sa bank account ng iba. Pero pagka po kasi cash, ibig sabihin, ayaw po ng trail. So kung wala pong trail, eto po sa amin yung mga telltale signs din po sa forensic investigation,” Cabrera said.

(You would need a bag for there. It is like they are chasing something. Everything happened in an hour. It could have been turned into a check or manager's check, then you will deposit that to another bank account. But if it is cash, you don't want a trail. Without a trail, that's a tell-tale sign.)
“Timestamp po nung huling withdrawal 12:23 p.m., tapos 1:17 p.m. Parang may hinahabol kasi right after lunch, tuloy ‘yung transaction. Matagal din po kasi magbilang ng P41 million,” Cabrera added.
(The last withdrawal came 12:23 p.m., then again 1:17 p.m. It is as if you are chasing after something, the transaction. Because it also takes a lot of time to count P41 million.) —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Ex-director who oversaw Grenfell cost-cutting leaves council housing role after backlash
articles.summary:
Survivors had criticised ‘outrageous’ appointment of Laura Johnson to £150,000 job with Barnet Group

A housing director who oversaw cost cutting at Grenfell Tower before the fatal fire has…

blocks.text: A housing director who oversaw cost cutting at Grenfell Tower before the fatal fire has left a £150,000-a-year senior council housing role after a backlash from bereaved families and survivors.

Laura Johnson was the director of housing at the Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea (RBKC) at the time of the 2017 Grenfell fire which killed 72 people;p, and was criticised in the subsequent inquiry for her role in budget-cutting decisions prior to the blaze.

It was found that she pushed for a new contractor to carry out the tower’s renovation works on a lower budget, which ultimately meant metal cladding was swapped for combustible plastic-filled panels to save money.

In August, she was appointed the director of development and property at the Barnet Group, which manages the borough’s 13,000 council homes, on a salary of £157,078, a move described by bereaved families and survivors as “outrageous and disrespectful”.
In a letter to Joe Powell, the Labour MP for Kensington and Bayswater where Grenfell Tower stood, the company confirmed that Johnson was “no longer employed by The Barnet Group”.

Eamon McGoldrick, the chair of the board, said in the letter: “We fully recognise the depth of feeling surrounding the Grenfell Tower tragedy and its continuing impact on bereaved families, survivors, residents and the wider community.
“We also fully acknowledge legitimate public interest concerning governance of senior appointments.”
He said he “owed obligations of confidentiality” to employees and could not go into specific details about Johnson’s situation. It is not clear exactly what led to Johnson’s job being terminated.

Powell said: “It’s totally inappropriate for any individual criticised by the inquiry to continue to work in housing, particularly while criminal investigations are ongoing. It’s right that Laura Johnson is no longer in such a position.
“The Grenfell Tower inquiry was clear about the failings of the RBKC and senior individuals involved in the management of their housing, including the tower.”

Last month, a Barnet Group spokesperson insisted Johnson was the “strongest candidate” for the role in a competitive field, and that it had considered her “professional experience, subsequent performance, references, qualifications and overall suitability for the role”.
A Barnet Group spokesperson said: “We can confirm that Laura Johnson is no longer employed by The Barnet Group.

“In common with any employer, we owe obligations of confidentiality to those working for us, applying for, or being considered for any role at any level. For that reason, it would be inappropriate for us to comment further.”

Last month the Metropolitan police said it had asked prosecutors to consider charges including manslaughter and fraud against 54 individuals, and 20 companies and organisations, in relation to the Grenfell fire.
The Crown Prosecution Service said charging decisions would be made before the 10th anniversary of the disaster on 14 June 2027.

articles.title: Sara Duterte: They’re rushing my impeachment because case is falling apart
articles.summary: 'Sabi ko, bumabagsak na 'yong kaso nila. Kaya binibilisan kasi wala na, wala na sila masabi. Nag-iimbento ka ng ebidensya,' Duterte says

blocks.text: VEEP. Vice President Sara Duterte waves to supporters as she arrives at the Quezon City Regional Trial Court for the arraignment of her grave threats case, on October 9, 2026.
Noel Celis/Reuters
'Sabi ko, bumabagsak na 'yong kaso nila. Kaya binibilisan kasi wala na, wala na sila masabi. Nag-iimbento ka ng ebidensya,' Duterte says

items: Vice President Sara Duterte has been cautious in commenting on her impeachment trial but recently claimed that the House prosecution team is rushing due to a faltering case.
Duterte criticized the prosecution for allegedly inventing evidence and highlighted that previous allegations against her have collapsed.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
Vice President Sara Duterte – at least in the last few weeks – has been conservative about giving comments related to her impeachment trial.

But on Monday, October 12, the Vice President dropped a fiery remark during the Office of the Vice President’s 91st anniversary. She said she believes the House prosecution team is rushing her impeachment trial because their case is faltering.

“Sabi ko nga kanina, sir. Sabi ko, bumabagsak na ‘yong kaso nila. Kaya binibilisan kasi wala na, wala na sila masabi. Nag-iimbento ka ng ebidensya. Sa simula pa lang, ‘yong impeachment complaint mo, walang annexes, walang attached pieces of evidence. Tapos gumawa ka, nag-i-invent ka ng ebidensya,” Duterte claimed on Monday.

(As I’ve said earlier, sir. As I’ve said, their case is falling apart. They’re rushing because they got noting, they have nothing to say. They’re inventing evidence. At the onset, in your impeachment complaint, you don’t have annexes, attached pieces of evidence. Then you are inventing evidence.)

Duterte is currently in the middle of her impeachment trial that could oust her from the vice presidency and bar her from running for president in 2028. The House prosecution team will soon wrap up its case because it will finish presenting evidence in three articles or allegations: grave threats, confidential funds, and alleged unexplained wealth.

The prosecution already dropped the bribery case, citing its “consciousness” of its impeachment timetable. But House prosecutor Jonathan Keith Flores said dropping it had nothing to do with the strength of the case.

Duterte, meanwhile, said her opponents were also pushing the allegations of self-confessed bagman Ramil Madriaga and the current claims of former cop Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. Both of these allegations, according to the Vice President, had already “collapsed.”

Madriaga executed affidavits tagging the Vice President in the Philippine offshore gaming operators (POGO) and confidential funds mess. Just last month, Gracioso alleged in his affidavit submitted to the National Bureau of Invesigation that he delivered millions of pesos to the Vice President when she was still the mayor of Davao City.

blocks.caption: The Gracioso affidavit: Ex-cop claims he delivered millions to Sara Duterte

blocks.text: Another fresh allegation against Duterte – in so far as her trial is concerned – is their alleged link of companies that do business with China. Senator-judge Risa Hontiveros, on October 6, revealed that Cale88 Food Corporation, linked to Duterte and husband Mans Carpio, received remittances from Chinese state-owned firms.
“Kaya nag-shift na ‘yong narrative to China-China naman tayo ngayon,” said Duterte.

“So ano ba talaga? Bawal ba talaga magnegosyo with China, kasi it is a national security risk? Parang nakakahiya na nga ‘yong drug haul na papuntang Pilipinas galing Laos and Thailand, tapos ito pa tayo na nagsasabi na ‘Naku, it’s a national security risk ang magnegosyo with China.’ Nagiging troublemaker of Southeast Asia tayo,” she added.

(That’s why the narrative shifted, we’re now on China allegations. So which is which? Can we not really do business with China because it’s a national security risk? It’s shameful because the drug haul went to the Philippines, from Laos and Thailand, and then now, we have this statement that “It’s a national risk to do business with China.” We’re becoming the troublemaker of Southeast Asia.)

blocks.caption: Sara Duterte: They’re rushing my impeachment because case is falling apart

blocks.text: “I don’t think the case is faltering. We are continuing… We will close the case today and we will wait for their evidence presentation,” said House prosecutor Terry Ridon.

The impeachment trial is far from over. Which also means the sub judice rule – the principle that bars parties and Duterte from publicly discussing the evidence of her trial – is still in effect. Remember, this is what kept the Vice President from talking about her case.
So did Duterte’s latest statements violate this rule?

“Tingin ko hindi naman na kailangan. Tingin ko tapusin na lang ho natin ‘tong proseso po na ito (I don’t think it would be necessary. I think we should just finish this case),” public prosecutor Terry Ridon said, when asked if the Vice President should be held liable for her latest statements. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Mining tycoon Joseph Sy to be released from BI detention under SC order
articles.summary: Immigration Commissioner Joel Viado says the release of Joseph Sy allows him to leave custody while judicial proceedings continue as ordered by the High Court but 'does not constitute a final…

blocks.text: Chinese national Joseph Cue Sy attends the Senate probe on Filipino citizenship, the legality of mining and other issues, on March 9, 2026.
Angie de Silva/Rappler

Immigration Commissioner Joel Viado says the release of Joseph Sy allows him to leave custody while judicial proceedings continue as ordered by the High Court but 'does not constitute a final determination of the questions surrounding his citizenship and identity'

MANILA, Philippines – Former Global Ferronickel Holdings Incorporated chairman Joseph Sy is set to be released from immigration detention upon meeting the Supreme Court’s conditions, the Bureau of Immigration (BI) said on Monday, October 12, while arguing that questions surrounding his citizenship remain unresolved.

Sy is the former chairman of publicly listed nickel exporter Global Ferronickel Holdings Incorporated. He was arrested at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport in August 2025 upon returning from Hong Kong after the BI alleged that he was a Chinese national named Cheng Zhong Zhen who had illegally obtained Philippine citizenship documents. The bureau cited a fingerprint match with its records of a Chinese citizen.

A Taguig City Regional Trial Court ordered his release in September 2025, but the bureau kept him detained while pursuing its appeal. In February 2026, the Court of Appeals ordered his release, citing his valid Philippine birth certificate as prima facie evidence of citizenship.

Immigration Commissioner Joel Anthony Viado said the bureau was now coordinating with the Department of Justice and the Office of the Solicitor General for the “prompt and orderly implementation” of the directive.

Viado said the case before the Supreme Court involves an appeal concerning Sy’s habeas corpus petition, which challenges the legality of his detention but does not touch on the issue of his Philippine citizenship.

“We wish to emphasize that the Supreme Court’s order concerns Mr. Sy’s release from custody while judicial proceedings continue. It does not constitute a final determination of the questions surrounding his citizenship and identity,” Viado said. “The legal issues arising from that investigation remain subject to judicial determination.”
Sy resigned as a director of Global Ferronickel in December 2025, citing “personal considerations.” He had earlier gone on leave as chairman following his arrest. – Rappler.com

articles.title: PAL suspends Riyadh flights until Nov. 29 after airport attacks
articles.summary: Flag carrier Philippine Airlines has extended the suspension of its flights to and from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia until November 29 due to the evolving security situation at the city’s King Khalid…

blocks.text: October 12, 2026 | 5:07pm
A plane of Philippine Airlines
Philippine Airlines via Facebook

MANILA, Philippines — Flag carrier Philippine Airlines (PAL) has extended the suspension of its flights to and from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia until November 29 due to the evolving security situation at the city’s King Khalid International Airport.
In a travel advisory posted on Facebook on Monday, October 12, PAL said flights PR654 and PR655 would remain suspended until the end of November.
The airline said it continues to monitor developments and assess conditions affecting the safe operation of its flights.
“Further updates will be provided as necessary,” PAL said.

The suspension follows attacks at King Khalid International Airport that left four Filipinos injured, three of whom remain in intensive care units (ICUs), according to the Department of Migrant Workers (DMW).
The fourth Filipino was expected to be discharged from the hospital. All four are recovering at different hospitals in Riyadh.
The DMW, along with the Overseas Workers Welfare Administration in Riyadh, is monitoring the condition of the injured Filipinos and providing assistance.

The agency also advised overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) in Saudi Arabia to avoid areas that could be targeted in attacks, including military installations and oil refineries. Those at airports were urged to stay away from crowded areas.
Filipinos scheduled to return to the Philippines were advised to contact their airlines before heading to the airport or check the email addresses they used to book their flights for updates.

Saudi Arabia is a major destination for Filipino migrant workers. It accounted for 24.1% of Filipinos deployed overseas from April to September 2025, the largest share among destination countries, according to the Philippine Statistics Authority.

articles.title: Erwin Tulfo shows NBI clips of Sara Duterte's alleged properties in impeach trial
articles.summary: Senator-judge Erwin Tulfo on Monday played videos from the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in the impeachment trial showing “resort-like” properties allegedly linked to Vice President Sara…

blocks.text: Published October 12, 2026 4:54pm

Senator-judge Erwin Tulfo on Monday played videos from the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in the impeachment trial showing “resort-like” properties allegedly linked to Vice President Sara Duterte and her family.
On the 38th day of the trial, Tulfo presented video clips from a press conference of the NBI, showing two big properties, one of which housed two swimming pools.

The senator-judge then asked financial forensic analyst Atty. Alexander Cabrera if the properties shown were declared in the Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN) of the Vice President.

“Ginoong Testigo, nabanggit po doon na may narinig po akong P200,000 daw po na halaga at mukhang agricultural land po ‘yan. Ito po ba ‘yung nakalagay na land agricultural sa Barangay Santo Niño, Balac, Igacos na acquisition cost ay P200,000 po?” Tulfo asked.

(Mr. Witness, I heard the amount P200,000 was mentioned, and it appears to be agricultural land. Is this the agricultural land in Barangay Santo Niño, Balac, Igacos with an acquisition cost of P200,000?)
The witness refused to answer, saying he could not offer an opinion off the cuff without assessing the materials provided.
“Dalawa po ‘yung ipinakita ho kanina ng NBI at lumabas na rin po sa mga media. Ang tanong ko po, kasama ho kaya ito sa P817 million pesos na undeclared wealth po ng Bise Presidente?” Tulfo pressed.
(The NBI presented two properties earlier, and these were also reported by the media. My question is, are these included in the Vice President’s P817 million in undeclared wealth?)
Tulfo was referring to the P817.87 million in allegedly undeclared assets and income by Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio, from 2022 to 2025, which Cabrera revealed during the trial on Friday.
The witness maintained he could not speak conclusively on that matter until he investigated the titles and other documents related to the properties.
“Kasi po baka isa po ‘yun sa mga property na naka-declare. Although, kung titignan ko po ‘yung pinakita n'yo, mukha naman pong valuable siya dahil dalawa po ‘yung swimming pool,” he said.
(It’s possible that they are among the declared properties. However, judging by what you showed me, it does appear to be a valuable property, given that it has two swimming pools.)
Tulfo clarified if the witness was saying that he was not sure if such properties were included in the P817 million he himself flagged.
“Tama po. Hindi po ako sigurado kung nando’n po ‘yan,” Cabrera answered.
(That’s correct. I am not sure if they were included.)
The senator-judge then asked the prosecution if the properties---which he described as resort-like---were included in the audit of Duterte.
House prosecutor Rep. Chel Diokno said they have copies of Duterte’s SALNs, but noted that he has never seen the videos presented by the NBI before.
“Would you later look into this to check, to counter-check kung tama po itong investigation ng NBI (if the investigation of the NBI is correct)?” Tulfo asked the prosecutor.
Diokno affirmed that the House prosecution team will look into the matter. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: UK politics live: Tories accuse Burnham of being ‘dangerous and divisive’ after he confirms Russian interference in Brexit campaign
articles.summary: Shadow minister says referendum was a ‘legitimate vote’ and PM is seeking to ‘reopen debate’ with statement on Russia’s involvement

blocks.text: Key events

items: 7m agoFarage says Reform UK would stop anyone being granted asylum for five years
14m agoEd Davey praises Burnham for confirming Russia tried to influence Brexit referendum result
32m agoTories accuse Burnham of being ‘dangerous and divisive’ after he confirms Russian interference in Brexit campaign

blocks.text: Farage says Reform UK would stop anyone being granted asylum for five years
Nigel Farage is set to announce a pledge to ban anyone from being granted asylum for five years if Reform were elected, the Press Association reports. PA says:

double quotation markThe Reform UK leader will announce a plan this morning to suspend the asylum system for a full parliamentary term and declare void any applications in progress. All asylum tribunals, legal refugee routes and resettlement schemes will be scrapped. A Reform government would not hear the around 90,000 outstanding asylum and humanitarian protection appeals and instead deport the claimants. The party would immediately close resettlement schemes that home secretary Shabana Mahmood recently said would reopen, with around a quarter of those admitted to the UK expected to be Palestinians and women and girls from Afghanistan. Reform says there is “no mandate” for such schemes and that anyone who has arrived under them would be deported. Any refugees granted asylum in the last five years would have their cases reviewed by the Home Office under the plans. Farage told The Telegraph: “The country is currently facing a national security emergency and the first duty of government is to protect its citizens. We cannot accept more asylum seekers while we still have no idea how many people are in the country illegally and the threat they pose. A Reform government will always put British people first and protect our borders.” The party will also pledge to use tariffs to force countries to take back migrants.
Summing up his announcement on social media this morning, Farage said:
double quotation markToday, I am announcing that a Reform UK Government will SHUT DOWN the asylum system. This is a national security emergency and must be dealt with.
Ed Davey praises Burnham for confirming Russia tried to influence Brexit referendum result
Ed Davey, the Lib Dem leader, has praised Andy Burnham for confirming that Russia tried to influence the outcome of the 2016 Brexit referendum. (See 9.28am.) In a statement, he said:

double quotation markI’m not going to agree with Andy Burnham on everything, but this statement needed to be said by a prime minister. After the Conservatives suppressed the truth for years, this took courage. We must do far more to protect our democracy from attack by the Kremlin and other hostile states, before it is too late.
Tories accuse Burnham of being ‘dangerous and divisive’ after he confirms Russian interference in Brexit campaign

Good morning. The last time Andy Burnham gave a statement to MPs after a recess, it went on for more than three hours. This prompted Kemi Badenoch to make a lewd joke later about the PM’s stamina (which she repeated at a party conference reception with an additional line about how she just had to “sit back and lie there”.) Today we are getting another post-recess, potentially wide-ranging statement from the PM, but the mood might not be so cordial.

Quite a lot has happened since MPs were last in the chamber almost a month ago, and they will want to ask the PM about issues like the cost of living, North Sea oil and gas, the Iran war and Ukraine. We have not been told yet exactly what Burnham’s statement will cover. But, as Aletha Adu reports, Burnham will talk about Brexit, restating what he told Labour’s conference about how he thinks it has done more harm than good and making the case for trying to find a better, closer relationship with the EU.
The statement will come after 3.30pm

Burnham has also given an interview to the Rest is Politics podcast and in it he confirmed that Russia interfered in the Brexit referendum. This is one of those statements, quite common in politics, which are simultaneously unremarkable and newsworthy. Unremarkable – because it has been obvious to anyone reading the news for the past decade that the Russians were trying to help the leave campaign. And newsworthy – because it is not something that any previous PM has been keen to say.

For some years ministers have been using the line – set out in 2020 in the government’s response to the intelligence and security committee’s report on the threat posed by Russia – that “we have seen no evidence of successful interference in the EU referendum”. That implies there is evidence of unsuccessful interference. But in the past prime ministers have not said that explicity. Post-2016 Tory PMs, whether they voted leave or remain, did not want to cast doubt on the legitimacy of the leave vote, and Keir Starmer was also reluctant to poke his stick into that particular hornets’ nest.

Burnham is taking a different approach. In his interview, Burnham was not asked, and did not say, if he thought that Russian interference had an impact on the result. Stephen Doughty, a Foreign Office minister, has been giving interview this morning and he told Times Radio:

double quotation markThe result is the result, and I think the prime minister has been very clear that he’s talking about attempts to interfere. The security minister has spoken about this before. I’m confident that both the British people and the British state are able to respond to and defend against these types of threats, but we need to be very honest that those threats exist.

(“I think the PM has been very clear” is the sort of thing a minister says when what they mean is “Of course, the PM wasn’t clear at all, but I’m happy to give you the line now.” Doughty later told LBC the Russians “haven’t succeeded in their many, many attempts to undermine our [democratic] processes”.)
The Conservatives have criticised Burnham for even raising the topic. Andrew Bowie, the shadow energy secretary, told Times Radio this morning:

double quotation markThat Brexit referendum was a legitimate vote. People voted in this country in record numbers to leave the European Union. And I actually think it’s very dangerous and divisive of the prime minister to reopen this debate in such an explosive fashion.
Here is the agenda for the day.
11am: Kanishka Narayan, the AI minister, gives a speech.
11am: Nigel Farage, the Reform UK leader, and Zia Yusuf, its home affairs spokesperson, hold a press conference.
11.30am: Downing Street holds a lobby briefing.
2.30pm: Pat McFadden, the work and pensions secretary, takes questions in the Commons.

Afternoon: MLAs (members of the legislative assembly) will vote on a no confidence motion in Michelle O’Neill, the Sinn Féin first minister, over her support for a protest against the proposed Orange Order march down the Garvachy Road.
After 3.30pm: Andy Burnham makes a statement to MP.
Late afternoon: Shabana Mahmood, the home secretary, makes a statement to the Commons on the safety of MPs.

I’m afraid we are no longer able to have comments open below the line every day on this blog. If you want to contact me, please email politics.live@theguardian.com. You can use this email to flag up corrections, comments for publication, questions or complaints.

articles.title: Frankfurt Book Fair: Rights lawyer Sands awarded peace prize
articles.summary: Franco-British lawyer and author Philippe Sands was awarded the German Book Trade's Peace Prize this weekend. Accepting the award, Sands criticized Germany's "inappropriate silence" regarding Israel.

image.caption: Accepting the award, lawyer and author Philippe Sands criticized Germany's 'inappropriate silence' regarding IsraelImage: Hannes P. Albert/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: The 2026 Frankfurt Book Fair concluded on Sunday with the awarding of the Peace Prize of the German Book Trade to the Franco-British lawyer and author Philippe Sands.

Sands was honored in the presence of German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier as a committed humanist "who, despite growing resistance, fights tirelessly for human rights, justice and mutual understanding."
The jury said that his work was based on a "commitment to the universal rights of every human being, evidenced in his advocacy for victims of war crimes, racism, torture and colonial injustice."
Sands criticizes Germany's 'silence' on Israel

Sands, a professor of law at University College London and human rights lawyer at the International Court of Justice in The Hague, used his acceptance speech to criticize Germany for what he called its "inappropriate silence" regarding Israel and its actions in the Gaza Strip and the West Bank.
Sands said human rights abuses should be clearly named, especially among allies, stating: "It's not antisemitic. It's not anti-Israel. It's the truth."
Philippe Sands: Peace through law

Sands, himself a descendent of Jews driven out of what is now Lviv in western Ukraine during the German occupation in the Second World War, became known to a broader audience through his 2016 book East West Street: On the Origins of Genocide and Crimes Against Humanity.

The work, which details the lives of two Jewish lawyers, Hersch Lauterpacht and Raphael Lemkin, and the origins of international criminal law, was translated into dozens of languages, including German as Rückkehr nach Lemberg (Return to Lviv) in 2018.
"Germany knows all about ethnic cleansing," Sands said in Frankfurt, referring to criticism leveled at Israel by many states over its treatment of Palestinians.
"So why the silence? Silence is not the way. Not for a family. Not for a community. Not for a country."

Sands also condemned the Hamas attacks of October 7, 2023, as "appalling" and "a monstrous crime against the norms of international law" and acknowledged that Israel, like any state, has a right to defend itself.
"[But] this right is not unlimited and must be practiced within the boundaries of international law."

articles.title: FACT CHECK: No new SC decision stopping VP Sara’s impeachment trial
articles.summary: Duterte's impeachment trial is ongoing; the most recent Supreme Court ruling dismissed petitions questioning the Senate court’s ruling on an adjusted conviction voting threshold

blocks.text: Claim: A new Supreme Court (SC) ruling has been issued halting the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

Why we fact-checked this: The Facebook reel bearing the claim has already received 79,000 views, 4,600 reactions, 1,100 shares, and 87 comments as of writing. It was posted on October 1 and continues to gain traction up to this date.

The video shows a photo of Duterte and the logo of the SC with the text, “Game over!! Basahin (Read) Breaking news game over na? | Supreme Court junks petition to force Senate to hold impeachment trial vs VP Sara Duterte.”

The person talking in the Facebook reel further claims that Duterte is set to replace Ferdinand Marcos Jr. as president following the SC ruling.“Good news sa lahat ng mga Pilipino, ayan basahin niyo. Wala na, game over na. Si Inday Sara Duterte na ang susunod na pangulo sa bansang Pilipinas,” he said.(Good news for all Filipinos, read this. It’s a done deal, it’s game over. Inday Sara Duterte will be the next president of the Philippines.)

The facts: The High Court did not issue any recent decision stopping the impeachment trial. The latest decision from the SC on September 30 dismissed the petition questioning the Senate impeachment court’s ruling that adjusted the voting threshold for Duterte’s conviction.
The SC unanimously dismissed the three petitions for lack of legal standing and prematurity, since the trial had yet to reach a final judgment.

The ruling allows the impeachment court to proceed on a basis that adjusts the number of votes needed for conviction, depending on the number of senators who can take part in the impeachment proceedings.

“Two petitions were filed — one was [for] a TRO, and the other was a prayer for status quo ante order. Both were dismissed by the SC, so that means the trial will continue… This also goes to show that the High Court respects the rulings of the impeachment court,” Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian said.
Exclusion of members: Article XI, Section 3(6) of the 1987 Constitution states that the conviction of an impeachable official requires the concurrence of two-thirds of all the members of the Senate.

On September 23, the Senate impeachment court amended its voting threshold. Instead of the Senate’s full 24-member membership as the baseline for determining the two-thirds vote needed to convict Duterte, the impeachment court ruled that it would only count the votes of senator-judges who are “legally and factually capable” of participating in the proceedings.

This effectively excludes senators who are detained, suspended, or restrained from performing their duties; whose whereabouts are unknown despite being sought by authorities; who are physically or medically incapacitated; who fall beyond the Senate’s power to compel cooperation; and those in similar circumstances.

Old SC ruling: The misleading Facebook reel is likely referring to an old SC ruling issued in April last year, which dismissed a petition that sought to compel the Senate to act “forthwith” on Duterte’s impeachment back in 2025.
The High Court deemed the petition moot as the Senate had already begun preparations for the impeachment. (READ: What does ‘forthwith’ mean in impeachment? SC defines in new ruling.)
The misleading video falsely framed this old SC ruling as a recent decision, but it has no bearing on the ongoing impeachment trial.
Previous fact checks: Rappler has previously fact-checked similar false claims about Duterte’s impeachment:

FACT CHECK: Chief Justice Gesmundo did not approve 13-vote threshold for VP Sara’s conviction

blocks.text: – Angelee Kaye Abelinde/Rappler.com
Angelee Kaye Abelinde is a student journalist based in Naga City, and an alumna of Rappler’s Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship 2024.

articles.title: NBI looking into Duterte family properties amid cash delivery claims
articles.summary: National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag said Monday that the agency was investigating properties linked to Vice President Sara Duterte and her family amid allegations by…

blocks.text: Published October 12, 2026 4:13pm

National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag said Monday that the agency was investigating properties linked to Vice President Sara Duterte and her family amid allegations by dismissed police officer Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. that he delivered cash to them.

“We’re investigating this because we are following the pattern established in the Gracioso affidavit. This means there is money involved, so where did the money go? It now appears that the money is being invested in land banking,” he said in Filipino.
Matibag said Gracioso’s affidavit pointed to a pattern of “land banking” among properties linked to the Velasco family, which the NBI was now examining in connection with the Dutertes.
“They engage in land banking. They buy land, build resorts, establish real estate companies and hotels, and develop luxury villages. This is the pattern we observed with the Velascos,” he said.
“And we are now looking into the same pattern based on the SALNs submitted by Vice President Sara Duterte doon sa real properties nila,” he added.

Gracioso had claimed that he delivered cash to Vice President Sara Duterte, Davao City Representative Paolo Duterte and former president Rodrigo Duterte on the instructions of former House Speaker Lord Allan Velasco.
Sara Duterte has denied the allegations against her.
Matibag said the NBI had identified 14 real properties listed in the vice president’s Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALNs).
“We asked our people on the ground to investigate. They will go directly to the locations and identify the properties that were flagged in the SALN,” he said.
Matibag cited agricultural land in Barangay Catigan that was allegedly declared at a value ranging from P437,000 to P450,000.

“There, this is one of the properties. It was declared as agricultural land. Its combined value is only around P900,000, but if you look at the resort, it is worth more than P900,000, and there is no declaration of improvements,” he said.
Matibag said the NBI would endorse the results of its investigation to the Department of Justice or the Office of the Ombudsman.
The NBI director also presented a property in Samal that was allegedly worth P1 million and supposedly owned by Paolo Duterte, also known as Pulong.

In a Facebook post, Paolo Duterte challenged Matibag to establish the facts and present evidence to support his allegations. He said he trusted that the NBI director knew the difference between a photograph and proof of ownership.
“The louder an allegation is repeated, the more important it becomes to establish whether it is true,” he said.

Paolo Duterte also said his father had raised questions about Matibag’s credibility. He added that the NBI director should show the same enthusiasm in investigating alleged ghost projects involving his wife.
“Director Matibag, I will not ask the public to take my word over yours. I am simply asking that you produce evidence and allow the facts to speak for themselves,” he said.
“If you have proof, present it. If you do not, the responsible course is to correct the record, not to mistake public office for a license to make accusations,” he added.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: DepEd lauds 5 students for bravery, int'l achievement
articles.summary: The Department of Education (DepEd) on Monday recognized five students for their bravery and achievements in an international competition.

blocks.text: Published October 12, 2026 4:11pm
The Department of Education (DepEd) on Monday recognized five students for their bravery and achievements in an international competition.

The agency awarded 14-year-old student Bryan Ezel Pamonag with the DepEd Heroes Award for his bravery during the school shooting in Banga National High School in Banga, South Cotabato last September 18, 2026.
Despite being wounded on the arm,Pamona locked the classroom door and blocked the window to allow his classmates to safely escape.

“Ang katapangan ni Bryan ay nagbibigay inspirasyon, ngunit paalala rin ito ng ating pananagutang tiyakin na ang bawat bata ay may ligtas na kapaligiran na malaya silang matuto, mangarap, at maabot ang kanilang buong potensyal,” Education Secretary Sonny Angara said during his speech.

(Bryan’s bravery is inspiring, but it also reminds us of our responsibility to ensure that every child has a safe environment where they can learn, dream, and reach their full potential.)Meanwhile, Pamonag dedicated the award to the students and parents of Banga National School as a testament to their collective resilience.
“Ang award na ito ay hindi na lamang para sa sarili ko. Inaalay ko po ito para sa kanila, sa kanilang pamilya, at sa buong Banga National High School,” Pamonag said.
(This award is not just for me but also to my fellow students, their families, and the entire Banga National High School community.)
“Salamat po dahil pinatunayan ninyo na kahit 14 years old pa lamang ako, hindi ako nag-iisa. Ang award na ito ay para sa katatagan sa pagbangon nating lahat,” he added.
(Thank you for proving to me that even though I am only 14 years old, I am not alone. This award is a testament to our collective resilience in rising above adversity.)
Authorities confirmed at least three children, including the shooter, died following the shooting in Banga.
International achievement

DepEd also awarded the first-ever DepEd Achievers Award to four students who won medals in the Spelling Bee, Debate, and Knowledge Quiz categories at the TeenEagle English Global Finals in London, United Kingdom, last July.
The students are Jamil Oumar Hataman, Mateo Antonio Sarandi, Prince Akram Qayum, and Mysha Mahreen Macabuat of Fountain International School in San Juan City.
Angara said this award is also a tribute to parents and school communities, who help students achieve such recognitions.
“This award is also a tribute to parents and school communities, a testament to what we are all capable of achieving together,” Angara said.
Meanwhile, Macabuat described the international competition as a “formative experience” that challenged them to “look beyond the classroom.”

“Attending and winning an international competition was a formative experience that challenged us as learners to look beyond the classroom and recognize what dedication and perseverance can culminate into,” Macabuat said. —Mariel Celine Serquiña/RF, GMA News

articles.title: Tito Sotto turns over SP office to Sherwin Gatchalian
articles.summary: Senate President Pro Tempore Vicente “Tito” Sotto III on Monday formally turned over the Office of the Senate President to Senator Sherwin Gatchalian, the incumbent leader of the upper chamber.

blocks.text: Published October 12, 2026 4:08pm
Senate President Pro Tempore Vicente “Tito” Sotto III on Monday formally turned over the Office of the Senate President to Senator Sherwin Gatchalian, the incumbent leader of the upper chamber.

Gatchalian assumed the Senate presidency in June 2026, after the ouster of Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano. Before Cayetano, Sotto served as the chamber’s leader from September 2025 to May 2026 under the 20th Congress.
In June 2026, Sotto was elected as Senate President Pro Tempore during a special session.
Based on the photos, the Office of the Senate President was turned over with the fixtures intact and some furniture still in place.

LOOK: Senate President Pro Tempore Vicente “Tito” Sotto III has formally turned over the Office of the Senate President to incumbent SP Sherwin Gatchalian. 📸 contributed photos @gmanews @gmanewsbreaking https://t.co/2JhsHQKG0Z— Giselle Ombay (@giselleombay_) October 12, 2026

Last week, Sotto’s staff were caught by surprise when the vacated office of detained Senator Jinggoy Estrada, the former Senate President Pro Tempore, was seen bare and stripped of furniture, sockets, and tiles.
The room was left bare with no furniture such as tables and chairs, and there were even exposed and hanging electrical wires and wall sockets removed.
Estrada’s office maintained that dismantling fixtures and other materials from a Senate office previously occupied by a senator is an “established and accepted practice within the institution.”
Representatives from the Office of the Ombudsman later inspected the office vacated by Estrada, according to Senate Secretary Renato Bantug.
Estrada is currently detained at the Quezon City jail after the Sandiganbayan Fifth Division ordered his arrest on non-bailable charges of plunder. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: How a loophole in Canada's species-at-risk law can leave wildlife in limbo
articles.summary: A new study finds a legal gap in Canada's Species at Risk Act can leave species waiting years for protection, with 153 of 288 cases overdue and still unresolved as of January 2025.

image.caption: A herd of caribou flee from a truck near Rivière-aux-Feuilles, Que. A new study found some caribou populations assessed as endangered have spent years awaiting federal listing decisions under the Species at Risk Act. (Rock Arssenault/Reuters)

blocks.text: A species can be assessed as endangered in Canada and still spend years waiting for Ottawa to decide whether to protect it — while the habitat it needs to survive keeps changing.

A new study found that of 288 species assessed as at risk since 2017, just 17 reached the Governor in Council — the federal cabinet body that makes the final listing decision — within the recommended timeline. Another 153 — more than half — were overdue and still waiting as of Jan. 25, 2025.

That includes populations of caribou, beluga whales and lake sturgeon that have been assessed as endangered or threatened while they wait for listing decisions that can trigger habitat protections and a recovery plan.

The researchers say the bottleneck falls in a gap in the Species at Risk Act (SARA). Ottawa has recommended timelines for moving assessments forward, but no statutory deadline for one crucial stage of the process.
The study doesn't say why the delays happen. Critics say the gap allows governments to put off tough choices between conservation and economic interests.

Peter Thompson, a postdoctoral researcher in biology at Simon Fraser University in Burnaby, B.C., and lead author of the study, said the government is routinely missing the timelines it set for itself.
"The government recommended one to two years, and they are consistently failing to meet that," he said.

A lake sturgeon rests along the riverbed. The Saskatchewan-Nelson River population was assessed as endangered in 2017 and has spent years awaiting a federal listing decision. (Eric Engbretson Underwater Photography/WWF-Canada)
The Saskatchewan-Nelson River population of lake sturgeon is one example. This ancient-looking fish can live for more than a century and grow up to three metres long.

COSEWIC, the independent scientific body that assesses wildlife, designated the population endangered in 2017 after declines of about 90 per cent since the 1960s. The study says it missed a recommended federal deadline for moving the assessment forward on Jan. 18, 2020, and was still awaiting the next step in the process five years later.
Thompson said the stakes are high because dams and other hydro projects have fragmented waterways and blocked the fish from moving between areas they rely on.
"It's preventing these species from going where they need to go to survive," he said.
What protection is delayed
A scientific assessment from COSEWIC does not, by itself, change a species' legal status under SARA. That depends on the federal government formally listing or reclassifying them.

Under the Species at Risk Act, listing an endangered or threatened species can trigger prohibitions against killing, harming, harassing, capturing or taking it. The law also requires a recovery strategy, which must identify critical habitat where possible. Once that habitat is identified, SARA contains provisions requiring its protection.

Those protections are especially important for aquatic species because SARA's core prohibitions apply to them across Canada, while for most terrestrial species they are generally limited to federal lands.

Drew Yewchuk, a lawyer and doctoral researcher at UBC's Peter A. Allard School of Law, says a gap in the Species at Risk Act can allow governments to postpone difficult decisions about protecting species. (Submitted by Drew Yewchuk)

Drew Yewchuk, a lawyer and doctoral researcher at the University of British Columbia's Peter A. Allard School of Law who did not work on the study, said habitat protection is one of SARA's most consequential tools.
"If the animals don't have habitat to live on, they don't live," he said.

SARA requires the environment minister to publish a response within 90 days of receiving a COSEWIC assessment. Once the Governor in Council receives that assessment, it has nine months to make a decision. But there is no explicit deadline for getting the assessment from the minister to the Governor in Council.
"It could just sit there forever because there's no timeline for the step," Yewchuk said.

Aquatic species stood out in the study. None of the 15 marine mammals or 49 marine fish assessed during the study period had been forwarded to the Governor in Council by the January 2025 cutoff. Ninety per cent of terrestrial mammals and 79 per cent of freshwater fish were still waiting.

Spawning sockeye salmon are seen making their way up the Adams River in Roderick Haig-Brown Provincial Park near Chase, B.C., in October 2011. Pacific salmon were among the aquatic species disproportionately affected by federal listing delays identified in the study. (Jonathan Hayward/The Canadian Press)
More than biodiversity

Andrea Reid, a citizen of the Nisga'a Nation and Canada Research Chair in Indigenous Fisheries Science at the University of British Columbia, said what is at stake goes beyond the loss of individual species.
"Because these fish are so deeply connected to who we are," Reid said. "It's not just food, it's all systems of tradition and culture and language."

The study identified 38 Pacific salmon populations delayed while the government continued collecting or analyzing information. Information collection was the most common explanation for delays examined by the researchers, followed by analysis. In 20 per cent of cases where the government provided an entry, no specific reason was given.

Andrea Reid, a citizen of the Nisga'a Nation and Canada Research Chair in Indigenous Fisheries Science at the University of British Columbia, says Indigenous consultation should be built into the species-listing process rather than treated as a cause of delay. (Talon Gillis)
Indigenous consultation was also cited in some cases, but Reid cautioned against treating consultation itself as an obstacle.
"It certainly does take time. That is a reality, but that should be part of the planned process," she said.
Reid said listing is not always straightforward for Indigenous communities because restrictions can raise concerns about continued access to culturally important species.
"We need species to be adequately protected, but we also need cultural connection to be protected as well," she said.

A beluga whale swims in Hudson Bay outside Churchill, Man., in August 2022. Several beluga populations were among the marine mammals still awaiting a federal listing decision as of January 2025, years after their latest COSEWIC assessments. (Olivier Morin/AFP/Getty Images)
Few answers for long waits
Thompson said vague or absent explanations made it impossible for the researchers to determine why many individual species were delayed.
"It certainly seems like there is, at the very least, a lack of transparency in what is happening," he said.
Yewchuk went further, arguing that the gap allows governments to avoid publicly choosing between conservation and competing economic interests.
"It takes the pressure off of them to make hard calls about species conservation and allows them to just let the issue slide away," he said.

Environment and Climate Change Canada acknowledged the gap at the centre of the study. "SARA does not include a statutory timeline for the minister to provide a recommendation to the Governor in Council," the department said in a statement to CBC News.

It said 76 terrestrial species assessed since 2017 had missed the government's recommended timeline as of Jan. 25, 2025, and that some cases require more time for public, industry and Indigenous input.

Fisheries and Oceans Canada said aquatic listings can be more complex. "For aquatic species, listing can trigger protections across all waters where the species occurs, because these species are under federal jurisdiction," the department said in a statement. Since the study's January 2025 cutoff, the Governor in Council has received assessments for 15 aquatic species, starting the nine-month clock for listing decisions. On Friday, the government proposed adding or reclassifying all 15 under SARA.
Thompson said the broader problem is the pace of the process.
"We need to make the system more efficient and get these species the protections they need, or at least get a decision more quickly."

articles.title: Amid public anger over housing crisis, Spain's PM takes bold gamble to secure majority
articles.summary: By making housing affordability the centrepiece of his campaign, Pedro Sánchez hopes to unite progressive voters while deflecting attention from other pressing political vulnerabilities.

image.caption: People light their mobile phones during a minute of silence for María del Carmen Abascal, whose eviction sparked nationwide housing protests, during a demonstration demanding political action to alleviate Spain's housing crisis, in Barcelona on Friday. (Albert Gea/Reuters)

blocks.text: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called a snap election on Oct. 5 amid unprecedented nationwide demonstrations over housing affordability.
The election, scheduled for Nov. 29, will bring Sánchez's parliamentary term to an end six months early, marking a bold political gamble by a prime minister known for taking risks.

The announcement followed the government's failure to secure parliamentary support for two proposed measures designed to address Spain's housing crisis. But a day after calling the election, the government approved the two decrees with some modifications. They include capping rents, a temporary ban on evictions and restricting companies from buying homes.

"It is only now, with protests and unrest spreading across Spain, that they have started paying attention to social housing and to the question of where people in this country can afford to live," said Sofía Olivares, 25, a student and spokesperson for housing advocacy group Derecho al Techo (Right to Housing).

While polls point to a right-wing victory, Sánchez is betting that the housing crisis will give him the political momentum needed to secure a parliamentary majority. Since becoming prime minister in 2018, he has had to rely on support from other parties to govern, as his socialist party has never held a majority in parliament.

items: Spanish PM calls snap election amid mounting housing crisis
Spanish pensioner Maricarmen, symbol of country's housing crisis, dead at 87

blocks.text: By making housing affordability the centrepiece of his campaign, Sánchez hopes to unite progressive voters while deflecting attention from other pressing political vulnerabilities. Chief among these are corruption investigations targeting his inner circle and the ongoing crisis in Ceuta.

This past summer, an influx of tens of thousands of migrants from Morocco reached the Spanish enclave. While most have since returned, thousands remain on the streets or in makeshift camps, overwhelming local infrastructure and fuelling calls from the right for stricter migration controls.
Thousands of Moroccan migrants leave after storming Spanish enclave
Protests follow eviction, death of senior
The housing demonstrations erupted following the forced eviction of 87-year-old María del Carmen Abascal, known as Maricarmen, who became a national symbol of the crisis before her death on Oct. 7.

In Madrid, protesters camped outside in scenes reminiscent of the Indignados, or 15-M, movement in 2011, an uprising that reshaped Spanish politics by breaking up the two-party monopoly and giving rise to smaller political parties.

María del Carmen Abascal, known as Maricarmen, 87, waits for police to arrive before being evicted from her home in Madrid on Sept. 23. She died on Oct. 7. (Fernando Sánchez/Europa Press/The Associated Press)

In Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, part of the Spanish archipelago off the west coast of Africa and one of Spain's most popular tourist destinations, residents have also taken to the streets in recent weeks to protest over housing.

Olivares, of Derecho al Techo, blames the regional government for placing tourism above housing. "It constantly holds back housing policies to prioritize tourism," she said, arguing that limited land and a lack of rent controls have further worsened the crisis.

Over the past year, families across the Canary Islands — one of Spain's poorest regions, where almost 30 per cent of people are at risk of poverty — have faced dozens of evictions. This week alone, the housing group has supported more than nine families facing eviction.

Sofía Olivares, right, of the housing advocacy group Derecho al Techo is shown at a protest to stop the eviction of eight families, in Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, Spain, on Oct. 7. (Sonia Håkansson Rivero)
"Property funds buy the buildings they live in, refuse to renew their contracts and throw them out onto the street,” Olivares said, adding that promises to rehouse tenants are often broken.

The lack of public housing is another major concern. "We've also been about 10 years without any type of social housing being built in the Canary Islands," she said, adding that more than 30,000 people in the islands alone are on waiting lists for public housing.

Social housing accounts for about 1.7 per cent of Spain's housing stock, well below the level in most European Union countries. The Bank of Spain estimates that the country currently lacks about 750,000 homes, a deficit expected to exceed one million by 2028.

Demonstrators calling for a change in the tourism model in the Canary Islands gather in front of beachfront tourist accommodations in Las Palmas de Gran Canaria on May 18, 2025. (Borja Suarez/Reuters)
Right-wing parties expected to win: polls
Right-wing parties have argued that Sánchez's relatively open approach to migration is placing pressure on Spain’s housing market.

Unlike many European leaders, Sánchez has argued that migration is necessary to sustain economic growth. Earlier this year, his government also launched a sweeping regularization program aimed at integrating hundreds of thousands of undocumented workers into the formal economy.

Polling points to a conservative coalition led by the People’s Party, alongside the anti-immigration party Vox, as the most likely outcome of next month's election. Such a result would bring the far right into Spain's national government for the first time since the country's transition to democracy in 1975, following Francisco Franco's dictatorship.

items: 'Absolute chaos' as thousands of Moroccan migrants breach Spain's Ceuta border
Why Spain is aiming to regularize half a million undocumented migrants

blocks.text: The People's Party warns that the rent caps proposed by Sánchez will backfire by driving homes off the market. The government's measures also largely failed to win the support of the real estate industry, which says they don't address the root cause of the problem: Spain’s structural housing shortage.
"We are trying to address a supply crisis without sufficiently increasing supply," said María Matos, head of research and a spokesperson at Fotocasa, one of Spain's leading real estate platforms.
"By focusing on regulating properties, rental contracts and landlords, we risk making it even harder to bring homes on to the market."
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez is shown at the Moncloa Palace in Madrid on Oct. 6. He has argued that migration is necessary to sustain economic growth. (Bernat Armangue/The Associated Press)

Fotocasa's latest data suggests landlords may already be responding to new housing measures. "In just eight days, long-term rental supply fell by 4.2 per cent,” Matos said. She warns that "measures designed to protect tenants can end up creating barriers for those still trying to find a home."

She also called for greater investment in public housing. "Since 2013, the development of new social housing has practically come to a standstill, forcing more households to compete in the private market."

Matos said she wants more land to be made available for development, alongside faster planning approvals. "We need to unlock public and private land, and speed up building permits to prevent projects from being delayed for years."
A man sleeps on a street near a protest calling for political action to address Spain's housing crisis, in Barcelona on Oct. 6. (Nacho Doce/Reuters)

Garazi González, 36, who now lives with her partner and their baby in an apartment building belonging to his family, said she has experienced the affordability crisis first-hand and supports the protests "100 per cent."

Four years ago, after renting an apartment in central Madrid for eight years, she saw her monthly rent rise from 800 to 950 euros (about $1,275 to $1,500 Cdn). Her landlady then proposed raising it to 1,500 euros ($2,400 Cdn).
"She said prices in the area had gone up and she couldn't keep charging me so little. She gave me just one month to leave," González said.

items: Spain could impose a 100% tax on foreign home-buyers as tourism drives up housing costs

blocks.text: "I know people whose rents were raised to push them out, or who live in fear of being evicted from homes they've lived in for years. Others live in gentrified areas where vulture funds buy entire buildings and kick everyone out."
Despite her disappointment with the current government, González said preventing the far right from returning to power is now her biggest priority.

"I'm not entirely happy with the left because they haven't done enough on housing or other issues,” she said. "But I want to prevent fascism from coming back. I care about protecting social rights.... As a woman and a mother to a daughter, I worry deeply about her future."

blocks.text: Here are the latest headlines and reports from across Germany on Monday, October 12:
Tired of missing our real-time updates? Click here to add DW as a Preferred Source on Google.
October 12, 2026
Söder: Those who voted for AfD speaker should show 'backbone'
"Do you want to go somewhere else? Then just say so," Bavarian leader Markus Söder said during an interview with public broadcaster ARD.

As a member of the CSU, the Bavarian sister party of Chancellor Merz's Christian Democrats (CDU), Söder was referencing bloc members in the state of Saxony-Anhalt who are believed to have voted for a member of the far-right in a secret ballot.
Last week, Tobias Rausch of the Alternative for Germany (AfD) — whose chapter in Saxony-Anhalt is classified as right-wing extremist — was elected state parliamentary speaker.
This marked the first time the AfD has seen a member elected to such a position, and the first time in postwar Germany that a right-wing extremist has risen to this rank.
AfD lawmaker elected speaker in Saxony-Anhalt

The populist BSW party had declared their intention to support Rausch's nomination alongside the AfD, but his win with 48 votes means that other lawmakers must have voted for him too. It is strongly suspected that these were members of the conservative CDU.

Rausch's election prompted outrage across Germany, including from CDU members who have accused their colleagues of abandoning the so-called "firewall" — the agreement amongst the country's mainstream parties not to support the AfD.
Söder called it "pretty poor form," from the CDU members in Saxony-Anhalt, saying they should "at least have the backbone" to make their decision public.

articles.title: Ombudsman: 39 flood control cases filed, more under probe
articles.summary: During his first annual report delivered at the Office of the Ombudsman on Monday, October 12. Remulla said that 35 flood control cases have been filed in the Sandiganbayan, while 4 are being…

blocks.text: October 12, 2026 | 3:36pm
MANILA, Philippines — Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla announced that the government has officially filed 39 court cases related to the massive flood control scandal.

During his first annual report delivered at the Office of the Ombudsman on Monday, October 12. Remulla said that 35 flood control cases have been filed in the Sandiganbayan, while 4 are being prosecuted in the Regional Trial Courts.
“Many more are under preliminary investigation and lifestyle checks,” Remulla said.
According to Remulla, these cases involve 52 individuals now facing charges. The high-profile list of respondents includes:

items: One sitting senator
One former senator
Four congressmen, including a former House Speaker
One former secretary and 33 employees of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH)
Eight contractors and other private individuals

blocks.text: Addressing the public, Remulla explained that the filing of these 39 cases was the result of a rigorous, three-step process with "no shortcuts and no exemptions".

The anti-graft office first gathered evidence— including contracts, audit reports, and physical site inspections— before presenting the findings to the respondents to hear their side, and finally filing charges once the evidence was deemed airtight.
“Our cases are not decided by trending topics, hashtags, or the loudest comment section,” Remulla said.

The Ombudsman then urged the public not to be misled or used by paid online operations, advising the public to seek the truth not in comment sections, but by examining court documents, filed charges, and presented evidence.
“May mga taong nagbabayad para sa comments, para sa reactions, para sa mga fake accounts, para pagmukhaing boses ng taumbayan ang isang kasinungalingan,” Remulla said.
(There are people who pay for comments, for reactions, for fake accounts, just to make a lie look like the voice of the people.)
“Kaya sa ating mga kababayan: huwag tayong magpagamit,” he added.
(So to our fellow countrymen: let us not allow ourselves to be used.)
